Adapted Out: He does not exist in the 2014, 2016, and 2023 movie continuities. Animorphism: Often enough to ato a better known rat identity. His equivalent in the mangaMutant Turtles, Yoshihama Takeshi, has a much more plausible name.

characters.name: Professor Honeycutt/The Fugitoid
characters.description: A'''fugit'''ive andr'''oid'''. A scientist whose mind was accidentally transferred into a robot's body, and is forced on the run by groups who would use his inventions for their own purposes. Usually a central figure of various "Turtles in Space'' story arcs, and an expert in teleportation technology. Adaptational Late Appearance: If he features at all it's typically after several terrestrial story arcs in most iterations. In the original comics he appeared as early as Issue #5 (not counting his own subseries that actually predates TMNT). Adaptational Species Change: Pre-Fugitoid transformation, he was aHuman Alienin the Mirage comics. In the IDW comics, he's a Neutrino. Then inThe Last Ronin, he's a plain old Earth-born human scientist. Badass Bookworm: Well... his original human form wasn't particularly badass, and even in the original Mirage comics he was an ineffectual wimp even after becoming a robot, but heTook a Level in BadasswhenThe Bus Came Backin Vol 4. In other adaptations, he's generally more badass, or at least Takes that Level a lot earlier owing to having a powerful metallic body at the very least. Brain Uploading: The most commonly accepted explanation for his existence, although doubts are eventually raised as to whether this is the case.

characters.name: Renet
characters.description: An apprentice "Timestress" whose job it is to oversee and protect the timestream. Tends to be the feature character inTime Travelstory arcs. Adaptational Intelligence: Slightly. While Renet is still a bit of aDitzin adaptations, she never starts out asToo Dumb to Livethe way her Mirage incarnation did. Adaptational Late Appearance: Time travel story arcs tend to feature late in most iterations. In the original comics she appeared as early as Issue #8. Adapted Out: The third live action movie prominently features atime travel scepter that looks very similar to Renet's.She herself isn't referenced directly however. Character Development: In fact, we're informed that her parents originally made her take the job as an apprentice timestress in the hope that she would undergo some much-neededCharacter Development. Initially a ditzy, irresponsible and overly impulsive girl, she eventually evolves into a mature, responsible and self-reliant woman — after having spent some time as grim-faced, solemn and reluctant. In the Mirage comics what makes it confusing is that, thanks to her traveling back and forth through time, we don't necessarily see this development in chronological order.

characters.name: The Foot Ninjas
characters.description: An ancient order ofshinobi, assassins and spies dating back to medieval Japan. In present day, they have semi-independent chapters all over the world, overseen by the japanese head council. Badasses Wear Bandanas: A villainous example. Several iterations (like theoriginalfilmtrilogyand the2012 series) depict Foot Ninjas as wearing red bandanas to go with theirall black outfits. Conservation of Ninjutsu: Ridiculously prone to this. A horde of Foot Soldiers are going down easy. The four Foot Elite? Maybe an even match for the four Turtles. The lone Shredder? More than a match for the turtles at the same time, unless they've undergone intense training. Cyber Ninja: The Foot Tech Ninja in the 2003 series, which grants them invisibility. Several series have foot-bots that are entirely robotic.In-Universethis makes them more dangerous andrapidly producedthan the human soldiers they replace, but in practice it's so the Turtles can destroy them without censorship. Cycle of Revenge: The Foot are honor-bound toavenge the death of The Shredder. The turtles ever getting a leg up on them usually just means even more are coming.

characters.name: The Shredder
characters.description: Oroku Saki (also known as The Shredder) was the leader of the Foot Clan. He is the main villain of the show. Shredder was frequently assisted by his Mutant henchmen, Bebop and Rocksteady, and was bossed around by Krang, until season 10, where he was replaced by Lord Dregg. Adaptational Badass: Within the show, he's aLaughably Eviland incompetent antagonist for the turtles. Within the various game adaptations of the series, though, Shredder becomes much more dangerous, lacking the often stupid plans he comes up with in the show, and proving to be a physical threat to the turtles. Season 8 sees him become a more credible enemy in the show however... whichstillmakes him this trope, as he's still a bigger threat to the turtles than he was in the Mirage comics, where he was the embodiment ofSmall Role, Big Impact, and the series'Starter Villain. Adaptational Comic Relief: In the original Mirage comics, he was a serious villain. In the cartoon, he is depicted asIneffectual Sympathetic Villainwith a much goofier personality and far more humiliating moments that he had in the source material (at least until the "Red Sky" episodes). Adaptational Intelligence: Unlike many other versions of the Shredder who rely on others' scientist works, and though he often uses Baxter Stockman or Krang's inventions, he is a brilliant scientist in his own right who designed alone Krang's new robotic body, and created many other devices and chemical formulas on his own as well. Adaptational Jerkass: In the original Mirage comics, his vendetta against Hamato Yoshi was to avenge his brother when Yoshi killed him over their mutual love for Tang Shen. Here, he's aCard-Carrying Villainand aBig Brother Bully.

characters.name: Karai
characters.description: A high-ranking member of the Foot Clan (in Mirage comics she's theleaderof the Foot). Her origin story usually involves her leaving her position in Japan to join the American branch of the Foot in New York, and playing a large role in the City at War arc. Often succeeds Oroku Saki as the Shredder after the turtles (apparently) take him out. May even share a close familial bond with him. Adaptational Heroism:InRise, she is unambiguously heroic, rising up against Shredder when the armor he wore corrupted him and turned the Foot Clan into a gang of terrorists. Adaptational Villainy: Karai in her originalMirageincarnation could best be described as being a neutral character who made a truce with the Turtles but still had her own agenda that she wouldn't reveal to them to maintain the peace. Most subsequent incarnations of Karai in the media, with the exception ofRise, tend to portray her as more of a straight up antagonist serving the Shredder with varying degrees of redeeming traits, and fights between her and the Turtles tend to be more commonplace. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul:In the original Mirage comics, she was the head of the Japanese branch of the Foot clan and had no other connection to the Shredder. In fact, judging by the existence of an adult daughter, she may as well have been older than the Shredder and his superior in ranks. Since the 2003 series, she has been consistently portrayed as the Shredder'sdragon, with the exception ofRise.In the original comics, she has no connections to any of the main characters outside of being part of the Foot clan. In the 2003 series, she is the Shredder's adoptive daughter. The 2012 series also follows suit and portrays her as the Shredder's adoptive daughter, with the added twist that she is Hamato Yoshi's biological daughter. InRise, she is the daughter of Oroku Saki/The Shredder and the ancestor of Hamato Yoshi and the Turtles. InThe Last Ronin, she is the biological daughter of the Shredder. In the original Mirag

characters.name: Bebop and Rocksteady
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: They're usually more formidable in the video games than the cartoons would have you believe, even when they're usually among the first bosses faced. Animorphism: Were transformed from humans to humanoid animals by the mutagen. In the Archie comics, this eventually starts influencing their mind. Bald of Evil: Rocksteady had blonde hair in his human form, but he inexplicably went bald after he mutated into a rhino. Beware the Silly Ones: Initially. They're stillDumb Muscle, but they'realsopretty tough and significantly stronger than the turtles, to the point that they could seriously threaten the turtles — they had to be out-thought rather than simply beaten up. Breakout Villains: They're not from the source material but they turned into very popular bad guys due to the '87 series that they came to be considered iconic and even integral to theTMNTfranchise. Many subsequent cartoons, movies, and comic books came to utilize the pair in new incarnations. And even some cartoons likeTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2003)that didn't use them had some sort ofMythology Gagto reference them, like in the episode "Samurai Tourist" where Usagi's rhino friend Gennosuke appeared and put on clothes that made him resemble Rocksteady while an evil boar, Kojima, antagonized the Turtles, making him reminiscent of Bebop.

characters.name: Foot Elite
characters.description: Elite ninjas of the Foot and the Shredder's personal body guards and lieutenants. All Asians Wear Conical Straw Hats: Consistently wear Japanese rice hats across all incarnations. Avenging the Villain: After the Shredders death at the hands of the Turtles, the remaining Elites swear a vendetta against both them as the Foot now fight for control over New York. Elite Mook: In all versions, they serve as the absolute best fighters of the Foot, second only to Shredder himself (and othernamed characters). Enemy Civil War: After Oroku Saki dies they strike at all parties involved in the war over the New York underworld, including the Japanese Foot. They are often enough rivals to Karai's claim over the Foot Clan in the initial power vacuum. Also rivals to the Demon Shredder in the 2003 series being loyal to the Utrom Shredder and (by that point) Karai instead.

characters.name: Shredder Mutants
characters.description: Hideously mutated clones of The Shredder, dressed in modified Shredder armor and trained to work as elite Foot soldiers. All There in the Manual: They are never named in the comics or the TV shows. Their names in the 4Kids websites and the toys are also different. The four-armed Shredder is called Multi-Arm Shredder in toy form, and Shiva Shredder on 4Kids' website, the one with large, monstrous crustacean-like claws is known as Claw Shredder in toy form, and Spike-Armed Shredder on 4Kids' website. The diminutive Shredder with a single, long wrist blade on each arm is called Mini Shredder on 4Kids' website. Big, Thin, Short Trio: Multi-Arm Shredder is huge and hulking, Claw is thin and lean and Mini Shredder is short. Body Horror: BIG time. Its probably a good thing they are never seen without masks.Claw takes it an extra notch, he doesn't even have HANDS, his arms are horrific, lumped pincer claws. characters.name: Krang
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: He's typically prone to sticking in the background in the show and doesn't often engage with the turtles directly. In the video games he's usually foughtnearorat the very end of the gameas a formidable boss with strong attacks and a lot of health. Adaptational Ugliness: Krang's android body is fat and somewhatGonkwith a disproportionally small head and arms that stick out at an angle. In contrast, the Utrom's android walkers were more balanced in proportion and also had synthetic skin to help them blend in with humans. Adaptational Villainy: Krang was based on the Utroms, a race of benevolent cephalopod aliens from the original comic who were stranded on Earth and seeking a way to return home and how like them, created the mutagen responsible for the Turtles' mutation. Bad Boss: He often insults Shredder and never hesitates to make his life miserable if he think he can get away with it. In the first episode of season 2 he sends Shredder to Earth without any supplies or soldiers, and in a later episode made him wait for supplies on a garbage barge just to annoy him. Also like Shredder he doesn't hesitate to abuse Bebop and Rocksteady verbally and physically and tried to kill Baxter Stockman because he didn't see any use for him in Dimension X, accidentally turning him into a fly mutant. Big Bad Duumvirate: Along with the Shredder, he is the main threat for most of the series.

characters.name: Rock Soldiers
characters.description: A race of stone humanoids, who work for Krang. Canon Foreigner: Created for the 1987 show. Mooks: Of Krangs's army. Proud Warrior Race: More like a proud soldier race, as their entire culture is about the military and discipline, and they are in a strict hierarchy. Rock Monster: They are all made from stone.

characters.name: Tragg and Granitor
characters.description: Two rock soldiers, who act as the army's leaders. Adaptational Badass: In most incarnations, they are as tall as humans and use weapons to attack. In the 2012 series, they are gigantic and have a magma body.While not to such degree, they are also more capable and dangerous in the IDW comics. While not to such degree, they are also more capable and dangerous in the IDW comics. King Mook: The biggest and toughest of the Rock Soldiers. Mook Lieutenant: The miliary commanders of the other Rock Soldiers.

characters.name: Baxter Stockman
characters.description: Mad Scientistand creator of the mouser robots. Never quite seems to remain whole (or even human, in some versions). Adaptation Origin Connection:Inthe 2016 film, he is the one who mutated Bebop and Rocksteady.Inthe 2023 film, he is the one who created the Ooze and dumped it into the sewers, meaning he is directly responsible for the mutation of the Turtles, Splinter, Bebop, Rocksteady, Leatherhead and the other mutants. Inthe 2016 film, he is the one who mutated Bebop and Rocksteady. Inthe 2023 film, he is the one who created the Ooze and dumped it into the sewers, meaning he is directly responsible for the mutation of the Turtles, Splinter, Bebop, Rocksteady, Leatherhead and the other mutants. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: In Mirage, he's a truly independent antagonist who doesn't have connections with the Shredder. In many subsequent adaptations Stockman is made into a henchman of the Shredder or the Utroms,though he may still have his own ambitions.

characters.name: The Rat King
characters.description: A man dressed up in rags and bandages who shares a rapport with rats. Varies wildly within incarnations—descriptions for each can be seen inthe other Wiki. Adaptational Badass: Depending on the incarnation, the Rat King can be either a man or he can be something more than a man with more superhuman attributes. However, in the IDW series, the Rat King is basically a god-like being amongst a pantheon of deities. Adaptational Wimp: The version of the Rat King seen inTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles & Other Strangeness, being based off of the character's earliest appearances in the Mirage comicsnoteTales of the TMNT #4, is the most mundane and down-to-earth incarnation of them all; he's just a crazy homeless person. He doesn't even have the"rat controller"gimmick of his other incarnations; he's just delusional and insists he's a monster. Ascended Extra: He was aMonster of the Weekwhodiedin his first appearance. Didn't stop him from becoming one of the Turtles' most prominent adversaries. He appeared in the '87 series just a year after his debut in the Mirage comics and the rest was history. Badass Longcoat: Wears one during his single appearance in the Red Sky seasons, "Wrath of the Rat King".

characters.name: Agent Bishop
characters.description: A chief agent of the Earth Protection Force. He seeks to eliminate the threat of mutants and aliens in New York and around the world making him at odds with the titular mutant heroes. Adaptational Personality Change: The original Bishop was fairlycalm and composed, and the 2012 series he's stoic as a Norman Kraang. In IDW he's far more deranged and prone to rambling, and in Mutant Mayhem she's much moreHot-Blooded. Adaptational Wimp:In the IDW comics hehas a severe deformity that leaves him helpless without aMobile Human Suit.In the Mutant Mayhem series she's more clearly middle aged rather than in fighting prime. In the IDW comics hehas a severe deformity that leaves him helpless without aMobile Human Suit. In the Mutant Mayhem series she's more clearly middle aged rather than in fighting prime.

characters.name: Slash
characters.description: AnEvil Counterpart(Though usually moreAnti-Hero) humanoid turtle, often based on a snapping turtle. His origins have varied greatly across continuities, being either a mutant of varying origins, or an alien. Aside from appearing as a twisted knockoff of the Turtles, another common feature is a fondness for palm trees. Anti-Hero: In most continuities, he tends to be this rather than an out-and-out villain, though he usually starts out as an antagonist to the Turtles. The Berserker: He makes Raphael seem mild and gentle in comparison. Brought to You by the Letter "S": He often wears a belt with a backwards "S" on the buckle. In the "Back to the Sewer" season of the 2003 series, Hun wears a similar belt with a similarly shaped Dragon and then inTurtles Forever,he mutates into Slash. Canon Character All Along: At least twiceIn the grand finale of the '03, original character Hun (a breakout in his own right by the point after 7 seasons of character development) ends the series mutanting into a humanoid turtle. After all his various costume changes, the one he's in at the time makes him look like Slash.A more direct set up is Raph's pet turtle Spike in the 2012 series which, is by all accounts treated like a genuineFurry ConfusionTeam Petin season 1, eventually gets hit with mutagen and changes his name to Slash in season 2.

characters.name: Mondo Gecko
characters.description: Adaptation Dye-Job: He has blue scales here. Adaptational Villainy: HeavilyDownplayed. Normally he is an ally of the Turtles and a good guy from the start, he is a member of Superfly's gang in this movie. That said, outside of his vocation he is not particularlyevilor evenmeanand gets along with the Turtles easily to the point they don't even treat him as an enemy nor does he in return even when they harm some of his friends accidentally.And on top of that, just like the other members of Superfly's gang, he redeems himself when the Turtles get through to them. Bear Hug: In season 2 of "Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninjas Turtles," Mondo basically latches onto anybody for a hug. Composite Character: He started as a Gecko like his Fred Wolf cartoon version, but his slimmer build makes him resemble the 2012 incarnation, who was a human turned Gecko mutant. Cool Board: Like all the other versions of Mondo, he is often seen on his board or holding it.

characters.name: Tokka and Rahzar
characters.description: A snapping turtle (Tokka) and wolf (Rahzar) mutated by the Shredder. Adaptational Badass: Rahzar's 2012 incarnation is much faster and more intelligent than how he usually is portrayed. And Tokka is an unrelated giantkaijumonster. Adaptational Intelligence: In the 1987 animated series, they are a lot more intelligent and eloquent than their live action movie counterparts. Adaptational Species Change: InTurtles Forever, they are human Foot Ninja mutated into humanoid animals, like Bebop and Rocksteady, instead of animals mutated into humanoid forms. In the 2012 version, Tokka is an alienkaiju. Advertised Extra: They appear on the poster ofTurtles Foreverbut are left unnamed and largely relegated to cameos in the film itself.

characters.name: Wingnut and Screwloose
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: In the toyline and comic books they were heroes and allies of the Turtles, but in their one appearance in the cartoon they're villains instead. Bat Out of Hell: Wingnut is an evil alien bat. Brains and Brawn: Wingnut is large and physically imposing but alsoan idiot, while Screwloose is clearly the brains of the operation but physically lacking. Mosquito Miscreants: Screwloose is a giant, evil, alien mosquito.

characters.name: The Punk Frogs
characters.description: A group of mutant frogs that may oppose the turtles before befriending them. Adapted Out: Only Ghengis appears in Mutant Mayhem, without his brothers. Canon Foreigner: Created for the '87 series. They would gain even more members in the IDW comics than the usual four (including the first true iteration of Venus after the much malignedNext Mutationseries). Heel–Face Turn:In the '87 show the were created by Shredder to destroy the turtles, but relented after they realized the turtles weren't so bad.In 2012 they wanted to wage war against humans, but Mike and Napoleon eventually made peace with them.In Mutant Mayhem it's just Ghengis who is part of Superfly's gang before they mellow out and become the Mutanimals. In the '87 show the were created by Shredder to destroy the turtles, but relented after they realized the turtles weren't so bad.

characters.name: Pigeon Pete
characters.description: Adaptational Intelligence:He's revealed to be capable of reading which he apparently used to learn human speech, and genuinely attempts to try and advise Leonardo after his fight with Mustang Sally. Adaptational Non Sapience: He seems to have no ability to speak when mutated in "Mikey Does The Right Thing", and largely acts like a wild animal.Subverted by "Leonardo Saddles Up", where if anything Pigeon Pete seems smarter than prior incarnations, turning out to have a large vocabulary due to reading the newspapers Leonardo laid down (not realizing they were for him to poop on) and genuinely attempts to advise Leo. Adaptational Skimpiness: While his version in theanimated series from 2012wore blue jeans and his version in theIDW comicswore colorful boxers. This version of Pigeon Pete does not wear clothing, after his mutation in Season 1. Subverted when he wears a brown vest in Season 2. Big Damn Heroes: When Bishop drops the Electromagnetic Pulse device, Pete flies in to grab it and take it high enough to discharge the pulse. Innate Night Vision: He is revealed to have this ability, as his eyes are capable of seeing infrared, detecting Lee's heat signature traveling rapidly through walls.

characters.name: Lord Dregg
characters.description: An alien warlord from Dimension X with aspirations to take over Earth. Stop us if this sounds familiar... Bad Boss: He ejects Hi-Tech into space in the season 10 premiere, leaves Mung to be swarmed by Nanobots, and absorbs the mercenaries he hired to gain their powers. Big Bad: He is the main villain for the last two seasons of the Fred Wolf cartoon, replacing Krang and Shredder. Black and Blue and Scary All Over: He has blue skin and what seems to be black hair. He shows himself to be aKnight of Cerebuswho can barely be considered comedic. Engineered Public Confession: At the end of Season 9, April manages to out Dregg as a villain by presenting a videotape of Dregg gloating to the Turtles about how the Earth will finally surrender to him and there's nothing they can do to stop him.

characters.name: The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
characters.description: Adaptational Name Change:Downplayed, but Donatello and Michelangelo's original nicknames "Don" and "Mike" are rarely used in the modern incarnations, and are almost completely replaced by "Donnie" and "Mikey". Although, the nicknames "Don" and "Mike"areoccassionally used in some newer installments likeTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin, but outside of the comic books, these nicknames are almost never seen anymore. Adaptational Heroism: Surprisingly, yes. While all versions of the turtles are unambiguously good people (er, turtles), co-cretor Peter Laird has stressed that the original Mirage incarnations (and to a lesser extent, the film and 4Kids versions) are not, as Donatello once put it, "guardians of society". They will help those in need if they happen to witness it, and they take handling the Foot Clan very personally, but otherwise they do not go out seeking wrongs to right. Later adaptations would make them more altruistic, regularly going out on patrols and looking for crimes to thwart. Badass Family: The Turtles and Splinter, undeniably so, as they are trained ninja and all. Badass Normal: In a sense. The Turtles are as physically capable as Olympic-level human athletes, but have defeated foes bigger, stronger, and faster than themselves. The only "turtle" abilities they invoke are the extra defense around their shells, advanced swimming ability, and the very rare occasion that they actually duck a limb in their shells to hide or dodge. Big Brother Instinct: The turtles are very protective of each other in every incarnation.

characters.name: Leonardo
characters.description: The leader who's always in control. Leo makes the scene to do anything it takes to get his ninjas through. Identifiable by his blue bandana and his twin katanas. The Ace: He is by far the best warrior out of all his brothers, beingStrong and Skilledand often makes the others look bad unintentionally, simply by being the most serious about his craft. This is seen in the third film, where his brothers fail miserably in horse riding while he masters it, making Don groan, "You know, sometimes, I hate that guy!" One episode of the 2003 show has Leo being the only one who was not caught off-guard after a blindfolded training session with Splinter, making Don say, "There goes Leo, making us look bad again!" All-Loving Hero: Even after all the betrayals and all the terrible things he's seen, Leo still expects the best out of people. Berserk Button: More often than not, Raphael is this. Especially when the latter disobeys him or mocks him for being aTeacher's Pet. Best Friend:Donatello. In the original comics. Because Raph is constantly challenging Leo and Mike constantly has his head in the clouds, the resident genius is the closest to the leader in blue due to his higher maturity level, loyalty, and friendly personality. It's also hinted inTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadowsthat Leo trusts Don a little more than Raph or Mikey.Michelangelo in1987 animated seriesfor these often pair up in their missions.Raphael in most other continuities. Despite their constant arguments and differing view points, Raphael and Leonardo are the closest to each other. In the 2012 series, Leonardo and Raphael frequently pair up in missions and sparring and like to compete with and against each other. In the 2003 series, Leonardo comes home after months of training with the Ancient One in Japan to find his family missing and his home gone. After spending an entire episode looking for a new Lair and his missing family, Raphael lets himself be vulnerable around Leo.Outside of the turtl

characters.name: Donatello
characters.description: The brains of the bunch, Donnie's the fellow who has a way with doing machines. He is marked with a purple headband and fights with a bo staff. Adaptational Jerkass: Whilst generally a nice guy, in some series, he's much less so:In the 2012 series, he is depicted as more neurotic and prone to outbursts and sarcasm. He also possesses a selfish streak when it comes to April in early episodes.Similarly in the 2018 series, Donnie is much more sarcastic with a heavy dose ofegoand difficulty expressing his emotions. He's still agood guy who cares and means wellbut he's definitely not as sweet as previous incarnations of the character. Adaptational Slimness: Post the franchise's acquisition byViacom, Don is often portrayed as astereotypically skinny geek, as opposed to histraditional appearancein the Mirage era.

characters.name: Raphael
characters.description: The angry one who's always ready for a fight. Cool but rude, Raph throws the first punch in every fight with the most attitude on the team. He wears red and fights with a pair of sais. Acrofatic: Not necessarily fat, but always the bulkiest when they have different body types. Not that it stops him from doing the same backflips and cartwheels as the others. Adaptational Personality Change: He is usually the angry,Wolverine Wannabelancerof the team, but the 1987 series and the 2018 series significantly changes his personality:In the 1987 series, he is a moresarcastic jokesterthan a violent guy with aHair-Trigger Temper.In the 2018 series, he isThe Leaderof the team, being the oldest brother in this version, who is fiercely protective of his brothers and is aGentle Giant. In the 1987 series, he is a moresarcastic jokesterthan a violent guy with aHair-Trigger Temper. In the 2018 series, he isThe Leaderof the team, being the oldest brother in this version, who is fiercely protective of his brothers and is aGentle Giant.

characters.name: Michelangelo
characters.description: The party dude who's got mad skills, Mikey's the one-of-a-kind wise guy and the most laid-back of the Turtles, who lists among his interests pizza, comic books, and more pizza. Wears an orange-yellow bandana, and duels with nunchaku. Adaptational Badass:Downplayed inTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin. Mikey was always a badass, but none of his incarnations can compete with the Ronin, who is a master of multiple martial arts and his brothers' weapons.Also hisFuture BadassversionSame As it Never Was, who is like the Last Ronin, but withan arm missing, while still kicking shell. Adaptational Dumbass: In the 2012 series. For example, he nearly got himself killed after eating one of Donnie's experiments that was clearly andrepeatedlylabeled "Mikey, don't eat". Also, hisNext Mutationincarnation, who nearly eats an important scroll Venus had at one point, without even checking what he is trying to eat and suggeststorching their own lairas an option to get Silver and his goons off the Turtles' case when it's discovered they plan on going through it during their escape and Splinter states that "to extinguish the fire, you must become the fire." Adaptational Jerkass: In theNext Mutationseries. To a lesser extent, in the 2003 series as well where he's more of a prankster than a slacker. Annoying Younger Sibling: He is usually depicted as the most immature of the turtles, with his antics often annoying his brothers.

characters.name: Splinter
characters.description: In shadows, Splinter taught them every single skill his sons need to be ninja teens. A mutated rat who serves as the Turtles' mentor and father, raising them from when they were young. Most incarnations choose one of two origins for him: he's either the pet rat of ninja master Hamato Yoshi mutated into a humanoid form or Hamato Yoshi himself mutated into a ratlike form. Amplified Animal Aptitude: In the versions where he was Hamato Yoshi's pet prior to mutating, he showed remarkable intelligence for an ordinary rat, mimicking Yoshi's movements to the level that he became just as good a martial artist as him after mutating. Animorphism: In continuities where he was formerly Hamato Yoshi, such as the 1987, 2012 series,Rise, and the Archie Comics. Big Good: He's this of the entire franchise and is both the father and mentor to the turtles. Butt-Monkey: He sometimes finds himself on the receiving end of his sons' antics, especially in the 2003 series.

characters.name: April O'Neil
characters.description: AGirl Next Doorwho serves as one of the Turtles' first human friends, and liason with the outside world. Normally associated with the color yellow, and an aptitude for either science or journalism. She's almost always introduced as aDamsel in Distress. Over time she'll pick up the basics of martial arts for self defense, if not become a full fledged ninja in her own right. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: In the original Mirage comics, the 2003 series andRise, she has a very familial and sister-like relationship with the Turtles. In the 1990 live action movie, the 2014 live action movie, the 2012 animated series and the 2023 CGI movie, her relationship with the Turtle is slightly less familial and she acts as aLove Interestto one of the Turtles (Michelangelo in the Live action movies, Donatello in the 2012 series, Leonardo in the 2023 movie and its spin-off TV show). Adaptation Species Change:In the 2012 series, it's revealed that her mother was experimented on and she's half human with some Kraang features.The original Mirage comic, rather controversially, revealed that she is actually a drawing brought to life by a magic crystal. The original Mirage comic, rather controversially, revealed that she is actually a drawing brought to life by a magic crystal. Adapted Out: She's appeared in pretty much every incarnation, with the notable exception ofNinja Turtles: The Next Mutation. What makes this odd is thatThe Next Mutationis implied to be set after the original movie trilogy, where shedidappear, sowherever she is during the series is a mystery.

characters.name: Casey Jones
characters.description: An eccentric vigilante who fights crime with various sporting tools (baseball bats, hockey sticks, etc.) Tends to have the most in common with Raphael. Adaptational Angst Upgrade: The 2003 show gave him a tragic backstory, that he didn't have inthe source material, where he was anAffectionate ParodyofAnti-Herovigilantes with tragic backstories and he was simply inspired to be a vigilante just from watching too much bad TV, likeT.J. HookerandThe A-Team. This backstory, however, wasadapted in the comics later onwards. Adaptational Villainy:InRise. The Foot Recruit, a young woman constantly fighting the Turtles to prove herself to the Foot Clan, is eventually revealed to be the show's version of Casey. She pulls aHeel–Face Turnat the end of the series. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: He is usually Raph's best friend, but in the 1990 film, he hangs out with Don the most due to Raph being in a coma. In theRisefinale film, he is closest to Leo. In the 1987 cartoon, he's simply an occasional ally and isn't close friends with the Turtles (nor is he romantic with April for that matter). Affectionate Parody: OfNinties Anti-Heroes(particularlyThe Punisher) according toWord of God.

characters.name: Klunk
characters.description: Michelangelo's pet cat, originally a stray that Mikey found and adopted on Christmas. Adaptational Dye-Job: In his few color appearance in the Mirage comic, Klunk was depicted with gray fur. The 2003 series turned him orange, and the comics followed suit — at least one Mirage comic published after the 2003 series depicted Klunk with orange fur on a cover, and the color reprints of the Image comic also depicts him as orange. In the IDW comic, he's white. Comic-Book Movies Don't Use Codenames: Inverted in the 2012 series. Michelangelo adopts a stray cat, but it immediately eats mutagen contaminated ice cream and becomes Ice-Cream Kitty, never once using the name Klunk. But true to other iterations of the turtles' cat, she still doesn't participate in the action and acts like a regular pet. That they keep in the freezer. Gender Flip: Possibly. Is male in the Mirage comic, the 2003 series flip flops from being referred to as male and then female after theBack To The Sewerredesigns. Ice Cream Kitty is also female. Replacement Goldfish: Mikey adopts one of the kittens Klunk fathered after his death. In the 2012 series Ice Cream Kitty itself is this, becoming theTeam Petafter Raph's pet turtle mutates into Slash.

characters.name: Tang Shen
characters.description: Yoshi's lover, who is murdered as part of his backstory. Adapted Out: Does not appear in the 87 cartoon orRise, though her name has a blink-and-you'll-miss-it cameo (where she's apparently the co-star of a Lou Jitsu movie). As Long as It Sounds Foreign: She's a Japanese woman, but her name is Chinese.Justifiedin the 2012 series where she explains that she's a quarter Chinese. Death by Origin Story: She's killed as part of Hamato Yoshi's backstory. Disposable Woman: Her only purpose in the narrative is to be Yoshi and Nagi/Saki's love interest and to get killed.

characters.name: Purple Dragons
characters.description: A New York street gang consisting of mostly teenage thugs, thieves and killers. Ascended Extra: Like the Shredder, the Purple Dragons were one-shot characters that appeared in the very first issue of the Mirage comics, though unlike the Shredder, it would be decades before they became a permanent part of the Turtles' rogue gallery. Most of their tropes were codified by the 2003 series. Adaptation Deviation: Their most drastic reinterpretion is in theRiseseries as a group ofcriminal teen hackers, rather than street thugs. They also lacked any major mob backer. Child Soldiers: Like real-life gangs, the Purple Dragons indoctrinate members as young as possible, preying on troubled and delinquent children who make easy targets. Depending on the Writer: What they look like, how effective they are as a criminal group, their overall ethnic makeup, their leadership, and whether or not they're just a bunch of thugs or they have more sympathetic qualities are all different depending on which continuity they're in.

characters.name: Hun
characters.description: Real name: Hunter Mason. A hulking, tattooed gangster who serves as the leader of the Purple Dragons street gang. Adaptational Name Change: He is introduced in the 2003 series, where his name is simply "Hun". When he wasadapted into the Mirage comics, he was given the full name "Hunter Mason". In the IDW comics, his real name is Arnold Jones andhe is the father of Casey Jones. Adaptational Nice Guy: Hun is still a Purple Dragon inTales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, but he loves animals and respects Mikey for saving a cat. Arch-Enemy: To Casey in most continuities. In the 2003 series, he killed Casey's father. In the IDW comics, he IS Casey's abusive father. His introduction in the 2012 series isA Day in the Limelightepisode for Casey where the two manage to squarely land themselves on each other's bad side permanently. Badass Normal: Like Casey, he's a regular human capable of keeping up with all kinds of mutant, alien, and robot opponents. Though has sometimesaccomplished wild feats of strength and durabilitythat border on the superhuman. In the 2012 series, he resembles anevil tattooed Bruce Lee.

characters.name: The TCRI Aliens
characters.description: An alien race that crash landed on Earth years ago. Or come from another dimension. They are usually the creators of the Ooze that mutated the Turtles. They resemble brains in jars and pilot humanoidmech suits. They were first called Utroms. The original Krang character only shares their design. Later "Utrom" and "Krang" would trade off as names for the species, or characters of the species. Whether they come from space or Dimension X would also be zigzagged depending on the continuity. Adaptational Villainy: In the original comics and 2003 they were neutral if not positive figures. Due to being combined with Krang over time this can shift.In the IDW comics, they are an evil race that conquered most of the galaxy, but due to wars and depletion of resources, they have been dying out. Krang is one of the few remaining.In the 2012 series, they are combined with Krang as a hostile race called "the Kraang" that wants toxenoform the planetand rule it.It's later revealed they were infact good until they were brainwashed by Krang. Now there's a resistance movement against him. In the IDW comics, they are an evil race that conquered most of the galaxy, but due to wars and depletion of resources, they have been dying out. Krang is one of the few remaining. In the 2012 series, they are combined with Krang as a hostile race called "the Kraang" that wants toxenoform the planetand rule it.It's later revealed they were infact good until they were brainwashed by Krang. Now there's a resistance movement against him. Adapted Out: They weren't included in the 1987 show, although their basic design was reserved for theCanon Foreignervillain of the series, Krang, who himself was not ever identified as an Utrom. Later series would use Krang as the name for evil Utroms of whichTheKrang may or may not have a direct counterpart.They were considered during the planning ofTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: The Secret of the Ooze,and may have even had atest scene filmed before being cut. characters.name: Committee To Restore American Patriotism
characters.description: A group of violent survivalists who got sick of waiting for the Cold War to turn hot and decided to force the issue with aFalse Flag Operation. In the 2003 continuity, they're instead an anti-alien militia. Dirty Communists: Skonk constantly rants about how evil communists have corrupted the pure American nation and how C.R.A.P will wipe the slate clean. Equal-Opportunity Evil: C.R.A.P surprisingly averts the racism usually associated with these types of movements; while most of the group consists of white guys, their leader Skonk is black. Fantastic Racism: H.A.T.E, the 2003 version, was formed in the wake of the Triceration invasion and specifically targeted aliens, or anything that happened to look like aliens. Fun with Acronyms: The original Mirage incarnation spells out "crap", presumably showing what Eastman and Laird thought of similar real-life groups.

characters.name: Leatherhead
characters.description: Adaptational Nationality: This version of Leatherhead sports an Australian accent as opposed to her previous versions which range from ambiguously American to Cajun. Adaptational Villainy: Much like in the1987 cartoon, Leatherhead appears to be an antagonist here.However, she and the other mutants, apart from Superfly, redeem themselves through the Turtles' persuasion. Ambiguous Gender: In most adaptations, Leatherhead is a male character, but this Leatherhead is voiced by a female actress. It was unclear how the character's gender was portrayed, as the note sheet in Baxter Stockman's lab has possible names for Leatherhead, including male names ("Erwin", "Tooth Daddy" and "Albert"), and even the toy box description uses gender-neutral language. The novelization and TV series refers to Leatherhead using female pronouns, making it a confirmedGender Flip. Awesome Aussie: Has the accent, even though she's not from Australia like her voice actress. The Bus Came Back: InTales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Leatherhead appears in a video, making this the first time any of the mutants from the movie appears in the show other than the turtles, Splinter, and Superfly's cameo.

characters.name: The Triceratons
characters.description: A warrior race of aliens that resemble anthropomorphicTriceratops. They may seek to make use of the Fugitoid in theirForever Waragainst The Federation. However the Tricertons also exist in series that make no mention of the Feds. Adaptational Species Change: In the IDW continuity the Triceratons are not an independently developed race but rather the creation of the Utroms via genetic manipulation of Triceratopses abducted in the prehistoric past, engineered to serve them as workers and soldiers. Later, they banded together with other peoples to rise up and overthrow their Utrom oppressors. Alien Invasion: At least one of their appearances in each incarnation (except IDW comic, where they came in peace) will be them invading Earth, be it for its resources, a tactical advantage, terminating their enemy and so on. Arch-Enemy: The Federation is their age old enemy. But among the heroes, they're often after the Fugitoid rather than the Turtles. Badass Army: Often, a single low-level Triceraton scout is one of the most dangerous fighters on Earth.

characters.name: Savanti Romero
characters.description: A monstrous time-traveling sorcerer intent on conquering the past, present and future. Arch-Enemy: Due to his time travel abilities, he's typically a rival to Renet and Lord Simultaneous. Deadpan Snarker: It varies a little how deadpan he is, but he's a bit of a wiseguy and a constant source of one-liners. Evil Is Hammy: He's probably the most consistently hammy villain across the TMNT multiverse. He loves to be big and dramatic, and put on a show for the heroes to show howawesomehe is. Evil Sorcerer: He can raise armies of dead soldiers to do his bidding.

characters.name: Mr. Braunze
characters.description: Chrome Dome PSI: Has a bald head and voluntereed in a mental ability enhancement program during the 50s.

characters.name: Clark Ashton Allard
characters.description: Did You Just Punch Out Cthulhu?: Manages to destroy Dagon by throwing it's summoning artifact into it's gaping maw. Yes,thatDagon! Expy: According toWord of God, he's loosely based onDoc SavageandThe Shadow. Our Vampires Are Different: Can't fly under his own power, instead using a technological flight suit, and supplements hisHealing Factorwith a stasis pod. Token Heroic Orc: Fights other vampires, and have apparently been doing so for a very long time. Unexplained Recovery: After destroying Dagon, Allard disappears without a trace and presumed vaporized in the explosion, only for the final panel of the story to show him in one of his healing pods.

characters.name: Traquer
characters.description: Fantastic Racism: Despises mortal humans and the fact that with their numbers and modern technology, they could exterminate vampire-kind, forcing the undead to hide in secrecy rather than prey on them like they used to. Suicidal Cosmic Temper Tantrum: Is willing to help summon anEldritch Abominationthat will more than likely destroy all life on Earth, vampires included, as long as humanity is wiped out too. Villain Team-Up: With the worshippers ofDagon, using the artifacts gathered byThe Whateley family.

characters.name: Old Man River
characters.description: Big Bad: Turns out to be the true villain of "The River" trilogy, and the one really commanding The Bloodsucker leech. Broken Pedestal: To the Indian warrior Abanak who has served him faithfully for years, only to discover that his "master" is just as greedy and selfish as everyone else who have exploited nature for their own gains. Elderly Immortal: He looks almost as old as his true age. Evil Luddite: The Old Man was a member of a technologically advanced civilization that destroyed itself some time during the age of the dinosaurs, with the survivors abandoning technology in favor of studying and controlling the natural world instead. They eventually discovered a kind of planetary energy that travelled along the rivers of the world, allowing them to transcend their physical bodies entirerly and become part of the river itself.According to the Old Man, there's other beings like him in every major water way of the world. For Science!: Despite his claims at having abandoned science, he still has the mindset of aMad Scientist, and intends to have Bloodsucker drain all the Turtles of their mutagenic blood so he can study it.

characters.name: The group as a whole
characters.description: Badass in Distress: Armaggon kidnaps Leonardo in part two of "The Future Shark Trilogy" and his teammates Shredder and Verminator-X capture 3 of the 4 future Turtles (only Future Raphael escapes).

characters.name: Wingnut
characters.description: Adaptation Species Change: In most other versions, Wingnut is an alien. Here, she is a mutant of animal origin. Adapted Out: Screwloose doesn't appear to exist. Artificial Limbs: Classic Wingnut, like some other classic mutants and anthropomorphic animals in general, had wings and arms at the same time, which already defies several natural laws. This version of Wingnut addresses that by having robot arms beneath her wings. It's also the reverse of some older versions of the character, who had normal arms and metal wings. Bat People: She is a mutant bat. Composite Character: She heavily resembles the extraterrestrial 1987 cartoon incarnation of Wingnut, but is a mutant bat like the IDW version.

characters.name: Craniac
characters.description: Brain Theft: Crainiac's M.O.; stealing brains from creatures who have led exciting or interesting lives and selling them off to aliens who wish to experience these memories.

characters.name: Sarnath’s Master
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: In the 1987 episode "The Incredible Shrinking Turtles" and subsequently the comic adaptation based upon it, the alien that the Turtles meet and bury in Central Park is straightforwardly portrayed as benevolent guardian who wants them to find and protect the Eyes of Sarnath from evil. In the comic, it is revealed that the alien is a member of the Mergia, a race who created, enslaved and ultimately abandoned a race of sentient robots known as the Triast. Sarnath is established to be the Triast who served the alien, whom he regarded as little more than his property. In a final act of spite, the alienstole all of Sarnath's eyesbefore abandoning the planet, leaving Sarnath to chase after him while totally blind. It also adds some ambiguity to his dying request to the Turtles. While he might have legitimately not wanted the eyes' incredible power to fall into the wrong hands, he also may have intended for the Turtles to collect themso that Sarnath would never see again.

characters.name: Cudley the Transdimensional Cowlick
characters.description: Big Damn Heroes: Happens a few times, especially in the Archie comic. When the Turtles are stranded somewhere desolate with no hope of rescue and no way home... guess who shows up out of nowhere to take them back to New York? Canon Immigrant: Cudley appears in the Mirage comics, not as that canon's version of Cudley, but asthe same Cudleyfrom the Archie comics! He's also debuted in IDW, but so far it hasn't been stated if its the same individual (although considering Mirage and IDW already share the same incarnations of Renet and Savanti Romero, the chances are good). Living Ship: A giant floating cow head who can fly through time, space and dimentions, carrying people in his mouth... or in some odd dimention inside his mouth. It's not really explained how it works. Nice Guy: Cudley's a friendly and laid-back sort who's always happy to help people in need. Stomach of Holding: Er, while it doesn't look like Cudleyhasa stomach, he can and has carried people somewhere in his mouth. Best not to think about it.

characters.name: Burne Thompson
characters.description: The boss of Channel 6 news. He's very bossy and dislikes the Ninja Turtles, though he allows April's reports to paint them in a positive light. Canon Foreigner: He was created for the cartoon. Characterization Marches On: In the first four episodes, he had a more tough-but-fair attitude. But starting with the fifth episode, he becomes theJerkassboss we're all familiar with. Depending on the Writer: Burne never likes Turtles personally, but sometimes he's aggressively against them, and other times Burne only gets angry with them if they mess with the Channel Six building or his reporters. Burne is at his nicest in mid season 3 to 4, due to the Turtles rescuing him in "Burne's Blues", conversely he is at his nastiest in season 8 starting from "Get Shredder". Da Editor: He gets on April's case for reporting positive stories about the Turtles.

characters.name: Vernon Fenwick
characters.description: April's cameraman, who is constantly trying to climb the corporate ladder and steal April's job. Asshole Victim: He often suffers humiliating misfortunes, but a lot of times he has it coming. Camp Straight: He's very effeminate and such, but he's sometimes implied to be attracted to Irma and in at least one episode tries to get April to kiss him. Canon Foreigner: He was created for the cartoon. Characterization Marches On: In season 1 he was friendlier with April, and helped her get the scoop on Krang's attack in New York even though she was in trouble with Burne at the time.

characters.name: Irma
characters.description: April O'Neil's boy-crazy best friend. She has a crush on Donatello, though shows interest in several male characters throughout the series. Accidental Heroine: She inadvertently defeats The Rat King by stomping on his foot when he refused to take her hostage instead of April. This causes The Rat King to drop one of his grenades and have to flee, saving April and the turtles at the same time. All Women Are Lustful: Irma's boy-craziness is one of her most defining traits. She is forever pining after a dream boyfriend, and always interested in the possibility of scoring a date. Species is no object, either. Apologizes a Lot: In "The Turtle Terminator", she repeatedly apologizes whenever she accidentally hurts Shredder. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: In "Attack of the 50 Foot Irma" she is accidentally enlarged by an enlarging ray powered by Exaporon, by Krang (who meant to fire the beam at Shredder). Upon being giant, Irma's clumsiness gets the better of her. Eventually, the Turtles manage to shrink her back to her normal size.

characters.name: The Last Ronin
characters.description: The last of the surviving Turtles and the titular "Last Ronin". Mikey was once the most laidback and fun-loving member of the turtles. However, after losing his brothers and master/father to Karai and her son Hiroto, he has grown into a much more cynical, vengeful, and cold individual who seeks to kill Hiroto as revenge. Adaptational Badass: Downplayed — Mikey was always a badass, but none of his incarnations can compete with the Ronin, who is a master of multiple martial arts and his brothers’ weapons. Afraid of Needles: He becomes nervous when April draws blood from him. Anti-Hero: He joins the resistance and fights Hiroto not out of heroism but to avenge his family. Blind Weaponmaster: InLost Years, Mikey spent a few years blind from radiation poisoning, but he received training from another blind master to compensate for his lost sight until his injuries healed.

characters.name: The Fallen Ninja Turtles
characters.description: Leo, Raph, and Donnie who one by one died at the hands of the Foot Clan, leaving behind their youngest brother Mikey. Their deaths along with their father’s kickstart Mikey’s journey to becoming a ronin. Divergent Character Evolution: Inverted. To preserve the twist of who the Last Ronin is, the turtles go back to having identical builds. Their ghostly forms hide what skin color they have, they do not appear with their weapons, and they are maskless (with the Ronin using each of their weapons and wearing a black mask). After the first issue and the reveal that the Last Ronin is Michelangelo, the ghost turtles get their colors back. Legacy Character: They and Michelangelo are succeeded by Yi, Odyn, Moja, and Uno as the next generation of mutant ninja turtles and protectors of New York City. Individually…Leonardo is succeeded by Uno as the team’s most dedicated practitioner of ninjutsu. Like all incarnations of Leonardo, Uno is constantly training even in his free time. While he and his siblings succeed Leo as practitioners of kenjutsu, Uno is commonly portrayed in side art favoring a single katana sword.Raphael is succeeded by Moja. While she and her siblings succeed Raph as practitioners of saijutsu, Moja is commonly portrayed in side art favoring a single sai.Donatello is succeeded by Yi asThe Smart Guy, specializing in mechanical engineering. While she and her siblings succeed Donnie as practitioners of bōjutsu, Yi is commonly portrayed in side art favoring the bō staff.Michelangelo is succeeded by Odyn asThe Heartof the team with anobsession for food. While he and his siblings succeed Mikey as practitioners of nunchakujutsu, Odyn is commonly portrayed in side art favoring a single nunchaku Leonardo is succeeded by Uno as the team’s most dedicated practitioner of ninjutsu. Like all incarnations of Leonardo, Uno is constantly training even in his free time. While he and his siblings succeed Leo as practitioners of kenjutsu, Uno is commonly portrayed in side art fav

characters.name: Master Splinter
characters.description: Absurd Phobia: Splinter has a fear of cats. Maybe its an instinctual thing, otherwise a 5 ft. mutant-rat ninja wouldn't have anything to fear from an ordinary stray cat. Adaptational Nice Guy: In theMirage comics, Master Splinter had trained the turtles for the express purpose of avenging his Master Yoshi, a big element in their arcs after their debut being them finding a new reason to live after fulfilling their mission. Here, he had trained the turtles purely for practical self-defense purposes and they wound up antagonizing the Foot Clan out of a mix of self-preservation and moral obligation. The fact thatthis version of Splinter is also Master Yoshimight have had something to do with it. Broken Ace:He's one of the best fighters and the wisest character in the show, but has his moments where his laments about his lost humanity weigh deeply on his heart with episode "Splinter No More" being a prime example. Cassandra Truth: While trapped inside Shredder's body, Splinter had a hard time convincing the Turtles about the whole situation. However, Splinter helped the Turtles realize that he was telling the truth through wise wisdom and the fact he was not willing to fight them. Characterization Marches On: He's seen eating pizza in an early season two episode. The series later established that hepersonally can't stand pizza.

characters.name: April Jones née O’Neil
characters.description: Action Mom: To Casey Marie. Artificial Limbs: April lost one arm and one leg in an explosion years before the events of the story and wears prosthetic replacements. Damsel in Distress: Just after Raphael’s death, she started spying for Casey and the Turtles on the Purple Dragons who were causing trouble in her neighborhood. Because April wasn’t fully trained yet, she was captured and had to be rescued by the Turtles and Casey. Died in Your Arms Tonight: She perishes in her daughter’s arms from injuries inflicted by Jigsaw. Hollywood Atheist: April believes religion was “designed to control the masses,” and other than a few visits to Sunday School as a child, she has never believed in a god.

characters.name: Master Sinichiro
characters.description: Breaking Bad News Gently: When Michelangelo arrived at his village, searching for Donatello and Splinter, Sinichiro calmly and sympathetically told him about their demise, calling them 'People, creatures, teachers, warriors, heroes, and legends'.

characters.name: Yi
characters.description: Yi is the mechanical expert of the team who likes to spend her free time fixing broken vehicles and appliances. Like her siblings, Yi wields a nunchuck, a sai, a katana sword, and a bō staff, but unlike them, she can control electricity. Barrier Warrior: Yi discovered her ability to make force fields out of electricity during battle. In-Series Nickname: Yi-Yi The Smart Guy: She’s the smartest of her siblings with a specialty in mechanical engineering just like Donatello was. Smart People Play Chess: Yi tries to teach Odyn how to play chess to no avail.

characters.name: Odyn
characters.description: Odyn is the muscle of the team, being the largest of his siblings. While Odyn is proficiently trained in various martial arts and wields a nunchuck, a sai, a katana sword, and a bō staff as well as his siblings, he prefers making friends over fighting. He has the power to turn himself into stone. Acrofatic: Odyn is the largest of his siblings but that doesn’t slow him down as a ninja. Justified in that his design is based on a snapping turtle. Gentle Giant: Crossing over withBruiser with a Soft Center, he is the largest of his siblings and a ninja in training, but he feels really bad for a Foot Synja that lost its head during training and would rather make the the two knight pieces in chess be friends than play the game correctly. Elemental Shapeshifter: Odyn has the power to make himself or parts of himself hard as stones. In-Series Nickname: Odie

characters.name: Moja
characters.description: Moja loves listening to heavy metal and frequently wears her head phones attached to a portable cassette player. While not as dedicated as Uno, Moja enjoys training in martial arts, and like her siblings, she wields a nunchuck, a sai, a katana sword, and a bō staff. She is very protective of her siblings. Moja has the power to read minds, have visions, and project her thoughts into other people which she and her siblings take advantage of to have secret conversations with each other. Big Sister Instinct: She is very protective of her siblings, especially Odyn whom she defends against Uno’s insults. Metal Head: She likes listening to Donatello’s old heavy metal cassette tapes. Telepathy: Moja’s mutation allows her to read minds and communicate telepathically.

characters.name: Uno
characters.description: Uno is the most dedicated practitioner of ninjutsu, preferring to spend all his free time training. However, he struggles with teamwork, often electing to do things on his own instead of following orders and helping his siblings. Like his siblings, Uno wields a nunchuck, a sai, a katana sword, and a bō staff, but unlike them, he has the power to change his skin color from white to black. Big Brother Bully: He calls Odyn fat due to his love of food and huge mass. Blue Is Heroic: Uno’s scales are a very light shade of blue, and he is raised to fight against evil and corruption. Chameleon Camouflage: Downplayed. Uno can change from whitish blue to black. Character Development: By the end ofThe Last Ronin II: Re-Evolution, Uno has gone from an uncooperative teammate who looks down on his siblings to good team player who values his siblings’ contributions.

characters.name: Casey Marie Jones
characters.description: Casey is the daughter of April O’Neil and Casey Jones. InTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin, she’s sixteen-years-old and the leader of a group of teenagers in Rock Bottom (New York City’s street level) who rebel against Hiroto’s regime. She found the Ronin passed out from blood loss and took him to his old Lair that she lives with her mother to heal. She becomes his student in ninjutsu and assists him in his final mission. InTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin: Lost Years, Casey, now an adult, mutates four infant turtles - Yi, Moja, Odyn, and Uno - and becomes their adoptive mother and Sensei. She trains them as the next generation of New York City’s protectors and mutant ninja turtles. InTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin II: Re-Evolution, Casey is the leader of the resistance against the Purple Dragons and other criminal organizations seeking to fill the power vacuum left by the Foot Clan. Action Mom: Promoted to one in the sequel when she adopts Yi, Odyn, Moja, and Uno. Dead Guy Junior: She is named after her father Casey Jones, who died before she was born.

characters.name: Oroku Hiroto
characters.description: Great-grandson of Oroku Nagi, grandson of Saki, and son of Karai, Hiroto succeeds his mother as leader of the Foot Clan at the young age of sixteen. For over a decade, he turns the Foot Clan from an underground criminal organization into a pseudo-military that took over New York City. He ruled the city with marital law, keeping anyone from leaving, until the Ronin electrocuted him to death while the Resistance defeated the Foot Clan. A God Am I: Hiroto rants to himself in Issue 3 that he considers himself a god. Bad Boss: After his men fail to capture the Ronin, he has the captain of his forces beheaded and his head fed to ravens. He threatens his replacement with same fate if he fails to find the mutant turtle. Later on, while sparring with his men, he tells them to fight him like they're trying to kill him, or he'll have them all executed. When one successfully strikes him, he kills him with a knife he had hidden behind his back. Badass Family: Hiroto’s grandfather is the Shredder and his mother is Karai, a deadly kunoichi. Then there is the entire Foot Clan which is made up of powerful ninjas that his great-grandfather seized control of. Big Bad: The main antagonist of the mini-series who succeeded Saki as the Shredder and led the Foot Clan to power over New York, and is the target of the Last Ronin's revenge quest.

characters.name: Oroku Karai
characters.description: After the death of her father Saki, Karai became leader of the Foot Clan. She forged an uneasy truce between Splinter and the Turtles but broke it when she ambushed them and injured Splinter. In retaliation, Raphael attacks her and the two lock themselves in a duel, ending in Raph’s death and Karai in a coma. Badass Family: Karai is a deadly kunoichi, trained by her father Saki, the first Shredder. Her son Hiroto is also a deadly ninja who takes on the mantle of the Shredder. Then there is the entire Foot Clan which is made up of ninjas. Even Evil Has Standards: As noted by the Ronin, she possesses some honor unlike her son. Master-Apprentice Chain: Oroku Saki trained Karai who in turn trained Hiroto. Missing Mom: It's never stated who or where Karai's mother was.

characters.name: Oroku Saki/The Shredder
characters.description: Saki is the son of Nagi, father of Karai, and grandfather of Hiroto. After Yoshi murdered his father, he tracks down Yoshi and Tang Shen to New York City and kills them both. His actions lead to the mutation of their pet rat Splinter and four infant turtles whom Splinter trains in the art of ninjutsu to avenge his Master Yoshi. As Long as It Sounds Foreign: Going all the way back to the Mirage comics, Saki is actually a feminine Japanese first name not a masculine one. Badass Family: His father Nagi took over the Foot Clan. He succeeded him and became the Shredder. His daughter became a powerful kunoichi in her own right and succeeds him as leader after his death. His grandson Hiroto succeeds his mother at the young age of sixteen and takes over New York City. Then there is the entire Foot Clan which is made up of ninjas. Missing Mom: It's never stated who or where Saki's mother was. This is especially poignant as his father Nagi seems to be too obsessed with Tang Shen to conceive a child with another woman. Posthumous Character: He’s long dead before the events ofThe Last Ronin.He only appears in a flashback in issue one ofRe-Evolution.

characters.name: Oroku Nagi
characters.description: Oroku Nagi was once the closest friend of Hamato Yoshi and the greatest warrior of the Foot Clan besides his friend. Unlike Yoshi, he was ruthless and desired absolute control of the Foot Clan which not even Yoshi was safe from. Their fractured friendship finally ended when theirlove interestTang Shen chose Yoshi over Nagi, starting the war between the Hamato Clan and the Foot Clan. Badass Family: His son Saki, granddaughter Karai, and great-grandson Hiroto are all powerful ninja who succeed him as leaders of the Foot Clan with special mention to Hiroto who also took over New York City and Saki who became known as The Shredder. Then there is the Foot Clan itself which is made up of powerful ninjas. Death by Origin Story: His death triggered the split between the Hamato and the Foot Clan, igniting a decades long blood feud. Crazy Jealous Guy: Nagi becomes enraged with jealousy when Tang Shen chose Yoshi over him. One night when Yoshi is away, he visits Tang Shen and forces her to choose him. When she doesn’t, he nearly beat her to death. Opposites Attract Revenge: Downplayed. He and Yoshi’s brotherhood was already nearly broken before they both fell in love with Tang Shen. Nagi desired absolute control over the Foot Clan for nefarious purposes which Yoshi would not allow. Any remaining semblance of their friendship ended when Tang Shen chose Yoshi, and Yoshi murdered Nagi in retaliation for almost beating Tang Shen to death.

characters.name: Death Worm/Olgoi-Khorkoi
characters.description: Olgoi-Khorkoi (also known as Death Worm) is the leader of Death Worm, a terrorist organization that spans from Japan to Italy and the main villain ofTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin: Lost Years. He is a callous warlord who’s indirectly responsible for a series of tragedies in the Ronin’s life which drives him to travel across Eurasia, train in various martial arts, and seek vengeance. To avoid confusion, "Olgoi-Khorkoi" will refer to the person while "Death Worm" will refer to the organization. Badass Boast: He calls himself "death" before throwing a sai at the Ronin: But for Me, It Was Tuesday: Death Worm's massacre of the village in Hokkaido, Japan disrupted the Ronin's peaceful life healing from his grief for his deceased family and sent him on a decade long quest across Eurasia to murder him. When the Ronin finally confronts their leader Olgoi-Khorkoi in Italy, he remarks that he barely remembers his subordinates ransacking the village. The Dreaded: Described by one of his victims as "all things evil," he is a callous warlord whose terrorist organization has massacred entire villages and tribes of people. For those that survive, they are taken as prisoners and sent to Boss Finn’s traveling circus where they are injected withbombs in their carotid arteries, and forced to fight each other to the death for Death Worm’s entertainment.

characters.name: Khuyag
characters.description: Flung Clothing: Khuyag throws his coat aside before fighting the Ronin. The very same jacket the Ronin took after killing him and his master.

characters.name: Abigail Finn
characters.description: Abigail Finn, or Boss Finn, runs a traveling circus/prison camp in Kazakhstan that forces humans and mutants to fight each other to the death for hers and Death Worm’s amusement. Adaptational Villainy: InTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2003), Abigail is a disgraced biologist and reality TV host that captures cryptids for her showMonster Hunter. InTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin: Lost Years, she is a terrorist that captures humans and mutants and forces them to fight to the death for entertainment. Continuity Cameo: Abigail Finn was originally a character from the 2003 cartoon series. Instantly Proven Wrong: She lets the Ronin go after his victory and telling him Olgoi-Khorkoi is in Italy, hoping her boss will kill him. Unfortunately, that doesn't happen as the Ronin kills Death Worm. "It" Is Dehumanizing: She refers to the Ronin as “it” and “thing.”

characters.name: Parker
characters.description: Parker is a doctor and one of Abigail’s subordinates in charge of injecting and removing micro-bombs from the prisoners of their traveling circus. Adaptational Villainy: InTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2003), Parker is Abigail's assistant and cameraman for her showMonster Hunter. InTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin: Lost Years, he is one of Abigail's henchman and a terrorist that injects micro-bombs near the carotid arteries of the humans and mutants Death Worm has captured in order to force participation in a series of death matches. Age Lift: In the 2003 series, Parker is a young to middle aged man. InLost Years,he is middle aged to elderly. Continuity Cameo: Parker was originally a character from the 2003 cartoon series. Mad Doctor: He is a doctor that injects micro-bombs near the carotid arteries of human and mutant prisoners. If any of them try to escape, the bombs go off, killing them.

characters.name: Tinker  2
characters.description: You Killed My Father: Tinker 2 blames April for the death of her father, but she still aides her.

characters.name: Professor Zayton Honeycutt/The Fugitoid
characters.description: Adaptation Species Change: The Fugitoid/Honeycutt is a normal human scientist from Earth in this continuity. Disintegrator Ray: Disintegrates Jigsaw, who shot April. Reveling in the New Form: Creates a new body out of nanobots and hard drive scraps on Roosevelt Island.

characters.name: Commander Avallone
characters.description: The Mentor: To April O’Neil Undying Loyalty: To April O’Neil

characters.name: Chormagan Noyan
characters.description: Chormagan is the chiefnoteNoyan is Mongolian for chiefof a tribe of Mongolian warriors. He accepts Michelangelo into his tribe and teaches him how to fight and navigate the world without his eyesight.

characters.name: Batu Bagatur
characters.description: Batu is Chormagan’s second-in-command. He and his men capture the Ronin and bring him to Chormangan Noyan. After the Ronin’s acceptance into their tribe, Batu assists Chormagan in teaching the Ronin how to sword fight blind and Gerel in assimilating the Ronin into their culture.

characters.name: Gerel
characters.description: Gerel is one of the tribeswomen. She is assigned by Chormagan Noyan to help the Ronin assimilate into their way of life. She becomes like a little sister to him. Heartwarming Orphan: She is a kind and caring teen girl whose parents were killed by Olgoi-Khorkoi’s minions. Like Brother and Sister: The Ronin calls her a “precious heart sister.”

characters.name: Amanda Rose Konnor
characters.description: A TV reporter, Amanda is the first human to be brought to the Lair and meet the New Ninja Turtles. Déjà Vu: Amanda is injured during a fight and is rescued by Ninja turtles who take her unconscious body to the Lair. She wakes up and becomes shocked at seeing the turtles. Substitute Odyn, Yi, Moja, Uno, and Casey for Mikey, Donnie, Raph, Leo, and Master Splinter, and this is howvariousincarnationsof April met the Turtles. She’s even a TV reporter just like 1987 April. Recognition Failure: Having heard stories about the turtles from her father, she initially thought the second generation were the original turtles Casey told her otherwise.

characters.name: Jiro Watanabe
characters.description: Evil Twin: The ending of "Re-Evolution" reveals he has a twin brother.

characters.name: Jigsaw
characters.description: Current leader of the Purple Dragons An Arm and a Leg: Has a prosthetic arm where his cybernetics are visible. Bad Boss: Jigsaw to the Purple Dragons. He lifts one of his followers by the throat for questioning him. Hero Killer: He fatally wounds April in their final clash, which results in her death. I Can Still Fight!: He uses his cybernetic eye to fight April after she took out his normal eye.

characters.name: The Turtles as a whole
characters.description: Adaptational Dye-Job: A much-needed change for the adaptation. In the original comic, the Turtles all wore red bandanas and were hard to tell apart (aside from having to glance at their signature weapons). The cartoon gave each of the Turtles their own distinct bandana colors, and all future adaptations moving forward would follow their color scheme. Adaptational Heroism: Although they were the protagonists of the comic, the Turtles were more morally grey in many areas. They were originally trained simply to kill the Shredder to avenge Splinter's Master Yoshi and most of their adventures afterwards were less about saving the day and more about a situation they were dealing with that affected them. In this, and all subsequent series, the Turtles are instead genuine do-gooders who use their skills to help people, not just people they know, regardless of whether or not the bad guy in question is a personal enemy of theirs. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: Their relationship is much less familial here. The turtles are friends and refer to each other as such. And their relationship with Splinter is more like master-student than the other incarnations where he is also a father to the turtles and refers to them as his sons. This islampshadedinTurtles Forever, where 87 Leonardo is baffled when the 2003 Turtles refer to their Splinter as "father". Badass Family: The turtles and Splinter, undeniably so. Beyond just being heroes in half-shells, they also go up against the Foot Clan, which consist of an army of robots all trained to be highly-effective ninjas. Then, they're led by one Oroko Saki, aka the Shredder, a master ninja and Splinter's oldest rival. And behind him is Krang, an alien brain from Dimension X who wants toTake Over the World. In spite of this, the Turtles consistently come out on top. Bizarre Taste in Food: Their pizza orders tend to be—ahem—acquired tastes. Some of their bizarre pizza topping combinations include marshmallow and pepperoni, peanut butter an

characters.name: Foster Fenwick
characters.description: Vernon’s eleven-year-old nephew with an IQ of 271. Broken Pedestal: Foster looks up to Professor Sopho and genuinely believes that he would never destroy the Earth. He loses all respect when he’s proven wrong. Child Prodigy: Eleven-year-old Foster Fenwick is a scientific genius, creating a device that throws the Earth out of orbit. Everyone Has Standards: Foster may be an insufferable genius with very little respect for everyone but Professor Sopho, but he firmly believes that “no true scientist would ever think of destroying the world” and will not hesitate to destroy his own invention to do so. Insufferable Genius: Foster constantly brags about how smart he is and looks down on everyone including other famous scientists but his hero Professor Sopho. He even deluded himself into thinking that the Turtles would want tomeethim because of how smart he is.

characters.name: Mona Lisa
characters.description: A human college student who was mutated into a salamander-like being and fell in love with Raphael. Aborted Arc: Although Mona Lisa appeared in just one episode, it was implied her storyline was just beginning. She may have been planned to be reintroduced in the eighth season, but this story was ultimately dropped in favor of the Lord Dregg and Carter storyline. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: After being mutated into aCute Monster Girl, Mona doesn't wear anything besides her scarf, belt and hair tie. Her yellow underbelly wasmistaken for a leotardin her original figure — as can be seen from the back — but this would be fixed in her later appearances. Adaptational Dye-Job: Most of Mona Lisa's appearances depict her withbrown hairand pink accessories, but her original action figure gave her black hair and red attire instead. Adaptational Job Change: In her original 1987 cartoon appearance, Mona Lisa was mentioned to have majored in physics. InShredder's Revenge, however, she's implicitly stated to be a chemistry major and even uses explosive liquid-filled beakers to attack. Given Mona's status as aGenius Bruiser, however, it wouldn't be too far-fetched forher to be an expert in both fields of science; something supported by how her 2023 action figure includes textbooks for both physics and chemistry as accessories."Mona is glad to return to her test tubes and beakers. But she'll always be up for another adventure!"

characters.name: Carter Dawson
characters.description: A college student who seeks out Splinter in order to gain some ninja training. He later becomes an ally of the turtles in their fight against Lord Dregg. Ambiguously Brown: He has brownish skin, but it's unclear whether he's African American or just has a tan, his hairstyle indicates the latter though. Cursed with Awesome: In his debut appearance, he gains a Hulk-like mutation power that sporadically causes him to turn into a huge, muscular yellow-skinned mutant with a metal arm and spikes. Magic Pants: Averted the first time he transforms, but played straight on all subsequent occasions where his clothes transforms with him. Only One Name: Carter's surname is never given in the show. That said,publicity and the old CBS website for the showsay Carter's surname is Dawson.

characters.name: Punk Frogs
characters.description: Four ex-pet frogs who mutated into humanoid forms after being released into a region of the Okefenokee Swamp in Florida that had been contaminated by some lost mutagen.
