Shredder tracked them down and tried to train them as his own elite mutant warriors to take down the Turtles. Unfortunately for Shredder, they were naturally docile, and defected from his side to become allies of the Turtles. The Dividual: Unlike the more individualized turtles, they all have the same mellow personality. Does Not Like Spam: They can't stand pizza. Dub Name Change: In Russian, Rasputin became Alaric. Hulking Out: The episode "Napoleon Bonafrog: Colossus of the Swamps" had Napoleon turn into a muscular behemoth when enraged after exposure to a ray invented by Krang.

characters.name: Zack
characters.description: A young boy who considers himself the "Fifth Turtle". Badass Adorable: He's literally brave enough to go inside a giant godzilla-like robot to save April, without even being fazed even once. He's also willing to face off against multiple villains to help save the turtles in "Night Of The Rogues" despite his young age. Inconsistent Spelling: Official sources can't decide on the last letter of his name being a "k" or an "h". Kid-Appeal Character: He's much younger than the Turtles and his immaturity is rather blatant. Kid Hero: He's managed to save April's life when she was trapped in a mechanical godzilla-like robot, and also helped save the turtles when they were captured in "Night Of The Rogues".

characters.name: Neutrinos
characters.description: A group of elf-like aliens from Dimension X who act like beatnik hotrodders. Their dislike of authority and war made them fugitives in their home dimension. Kala, the female of the group, develops a crush on Michelangelo. Actual Pacifist: Their defining trait is that they hate war and want to play instead, which is illegal in Dimension X.Technical Pacifist: Although they do use weapons to defend themselves. Subverted when Dask reveals in the episode "Hot Rodding Teenagers" that the weapons on their automobiles are required by law. Technical Pacifist: Although they do use weapons to defend themselves. Subverted when Dask reveals in the episode "Hot Rodding Teenagers" that the weapons on their automobiles are required by law. Anime Hair: To insane degrees. Beatnik: Their whole gimmick revolves around being alien beatniks, complete with the lingo.Dask:Cool? Daddy-o, we arefrozen!

characters.name: Muck Man and Joe Eyeball
characters.description: A pair of garbage men who were turned into junk and detritus-themed mutants, after Bebop and Rocksteady accidentally dumped a mutagen called Compound-X on them. Abhorrent Admirer: Joe Eyeball became smitten with Irma when he first saw her, but she's understandably repulsed by his mutated appearance to his disappointment (although she did compliment his eyes). Abnormal Ammo: They fight by throwing slimy garbage balls. Aborted Arc: At the end of their single episode appearance, Donatello promised that he'd try to find a cure for their mutation someday, but they told him to take his time as they genuinely liked being mutant superheroes. Alliterative Name: Besides the obvious, both of the garbage men had one prior to their mutation: Muck Man was Garson Grunge, and Joe Eyeball was Joe Junkee.

characters.name: Usagi Yojimbo
characters.description: A rabbit samurai from an alternate universe. Aborted Arc: By his second (and final) appearance in the series, the matter of him being trapped in the turtles' dimension wasn't resolved. This would finally be addressed in a one-shot crossover forSaturday Morning Adventures, which sees him return to his universe and the turtles exploring it at the same time. Adaptation Name Change: In the 1987 animated series, he is named Usagi Yojimbo - Yojimbo (bodyguard) is hisjob, not his name. His actual name in the original comic series (which is titledUsagi Yojimbo) is Miyamoto Usagi. Adaptation Personality Change: He's more emotional in the show than he is in his comics, where he was more in control of his emotions. Bilingual Bonus: His name is Japanese for "Rabbit Bodyguard".

characters.name: Foot Soldiers
characters.description: Conservation of Ninjutsu: Ridiculously prone to this. The Turtles plow through them with ease even when the Foot Soldiers outnumber them. Justified asdue to being robotsthe Turtles don't have to hold back and can mow them down in droves. Faceless Goons: The rank and file ninjas have virtually no defining characteristics. Mecha-Mooks: They're mindless robots, which gets around the moral dilemma of the Turtles mowing down human soldiers. Shredder and Krang once tried to create a Foot Soldier that could think for itself, but the result, Alpha One, ended uprebelling against them. Ninja: They are ninjas — robot ninjas, specifically. The Voiceless: Due to not having sapience, they never speak, except for Alpha-One.

characters.name: The Hi-Tech
characters.description: The Dragon: He is Dregg's right-hand until the premier of Season 10, where Dregg shoots him into space as punishment forfailing him one time too many. Insectoid Aliens: He appears to be a slightly cybernetic insectoid. Satellite Character: He mainly acts as a competent minion to Dregg without any other notable characterstics. Thrown Out the Airlock: His chair is shot out of an airlock once Dregg has no more use for him.

characters.name: Mung
characters.description: Hi Tech's replacement in Season 10. The Dragon: Dregg named him his new second in command, thenlaunched Hi-Tech into space. Fat Bastard: It's only natural considering he's also aVillainous Gluttonas well. Villainous Glutton: As shown in "The Power of Three", where he is seen eating a lot of slimy food. Dregg exasperatedly points out that he'd get things done faster if he didn't spend as much time eating. You Have Outlived Your Usefulness: In thefinal episode of the series, "Divide and Conquer", Lord Dregg leaves Mung for dead after gaining the power needed to defeat the Turtles.

characters.name: Titanus
characters.description: The leader of the organization H.A.V.O.C., he's a mutant who traveled to the present day from the future to take it over while humanity was much more vulnerable. Arc Villain: He shows up for three episodes in the middle of season 8, then after he's defeated Shredder returns and serves as the main villain again for the rest of the season. Fat Bastard: He's extremely corpulent and not a pleasant person at all. Non-Action Big Bad: He leaves the fighting to the mutants he creates. Not-So-Well-Intentioned Extremist: He and his organization claim to protect mutants shunned by humans; Donatello and Raphael, sick of beingHeroes With Bad Publicityanddealing with the ingratitude of humans, decide to join them… until they discover H.A.V.O.C. mutating a captive man and realize their real goal is to mutate people to dominate humanity completely.

characters.name: Don Turtelli
characters.description: The head of a major crime syndicate in New York. He is the grandson of Tony "The Tickler" Turtelli. Turtelli went down in infamy for his torture methods, which he inherited from his grandfather. He specializes in the interrogation of people he captures through tickle torturing the soles of his victims' feet with a feather to make them talk Including April, Vernon, Zach and his friend Caitlyn. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He's never seen or heard from again after the third season. Most jarringly, when Shredder unites the other prominent gangster villains on the show such as PinkyMcFingersand Big Louie in "Adventures in Turtle-Sitting", Turtelli is conspicuously unmentioned. Dirty Old Man: His addressing to Caitlyn with the question "Where do you want it, Blondie; under your arm or the soles of your feet?" confirms this. The Family for the Whole Family: He's a gangster who has a distinctly child-friendly way of operating, such as interrogating people withTickle Torture. Only Bad Guys Call Their Lawyers: Says this after the Turtles defeat him in the episode "The Great Boldini".

characters.name: Big Louie
characters.description: Another gangster antagonist who first shows up in the fourth season. Toyless Toyline Character: He doesn't have any figures Villain Team-Up: He often joins forces with the Shredder.

characters.name: PinkyMcFingers
characters.description: McFingersis another recurring gangster antagonist on the show, who like Big Louie first appears in Season 4. Toyless Toyline Character: Like Turtelli and Louie, he doesn't have a figure in the toyline.

characters.name: Lotus Blossom
characters.description: A mercenary hired by Krang. The Ace: Anyone able to hold their own against bothLeonardoandShredderwithout any issues easily qualifies for this. Always Someone Better: She easily beatsLeonardoin a duel during their first encounter. Beauty Is Bad: Initially downplayed until herHeel–Face Turn, as Lotus is very beautiful and starts off as an antagonist but sheisn't inherently eviland only assists Krang becauseshe wanted her payment.When Krang learns that she developed feelings for Leonardo, he takes away her pay leading to her helping the turtles and Splinter stop the villains and cementing her role as an ally to the turtles. Broken Ace: She becomes this in her second appearance, as she realizes with all of her ninja skills and abilities, she really doesn't fit in modern society.

characters.name: Dirtbag and Groundchuck
characters.description: A mole and bull who were accidentally mutated by Bebop and Rocksteady in "Planet of the Turtleoids". The Berserker: They are aggressive and short-tempered brutes who won't hesitate to attack anyone who bothers them. Co-Dragons: Their final appearance had them become minions of aSpace Piratenamed Captain Dredd. For the Evulz: When Shredder orders Groundchuck and Dirtbag to help steal a ruby after they are mutated, Groundchuck replies that he'd rather just tear stuff apart, and Dirtbag agrees. The two then pummel Shredder, Rocksteady, and Bebop and depart. Informed Species: Dirtbag looks more like a rat than any kind of mole.

characters.name: Chronos
characters.description: He used to be a man named Winston Fripp. He robbed a bank only to be captured by the Turtles and left tied up in a clock tower for the police. It was hours before the police found him, and by then he was driven insane by the ticking of the clock and the ringing of the bell. He returned years later as the supervillain Chronos to help Dregg defeat the Turtles. Ax-Crazy: He's clearly not mentally stable. From Nobody to Nightmare: He was originally just a petty thief, but now tries to best the Turtles in a game of wits. Large Ham: He's very expressive and melodramatic. Monster of the Week: He only appeared in one episode.

characters.name: Glob Father
characters.description: You Have Failed Me: Reduces a crony to a puddle of slime on screen for failing to steal the Protein Computer, telling said crony that nobody fails him (The Glob Father) twice. He then says that anyone else who fails him will suffer the same fate.

characters.name: Charles Pennington
characters.description: April O'Neil's boss at Channel 3 News. Canon Immigrant: Was eventually featured in theMirage comics. Papa Wolf: Charles proves to be one.Chief Sterns offers to expunge Danny's criminal record if Charles will get April to back off the crime wave story. After unsuccessfully attempting to get her to drop it, Charles fires her as a last resort, proving he's willing to lose his top reporter if it means a second chance and a clean slate for his son. Reasonable Authority Figure: He's competent in doing his job as Channel 3's news editor and genuinely cares for the well-being of AprilandDanny. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: For Burne Thompson (as April's boss at the news station). He is more pleasant, however, actually being concerned for the safety of his son as well as April.

characters.name: Danny
characters.description: The son of Charles Pennington. Secretly part of the Foot Clan. Canon Foreigner: He was created for the first movie and never appeared in the comics. Delinquent: His issues with his dad Charles caused him to think his dad didn't love him and he started stealing for the Foot. When confronted by his dad about it, he ran off.Charles:I make more than enough money to provide for the both of us and you're stealing. Why?Danny:I don't know.Charles:You don't know?! [scoffs] What the heck were you doin' with a car stereo anyway?Or, uh, don't you know that either?Danny:Sorry!Charles:Sorry? Not as sorry as you're gonna be after school. Headphones Equal Isolation: Noticed by his dad, which annoys him. Heel Realization: Starts when he sees Tatsu violently beat other members for failing, but crystalizes when he learns the full details of who Shredder really is.

characters.name: Professor Perry
characters.description: One of the lead scientists at T.G.R.I., he was the overseer for the mutagen disposal project. He is kidnapped by Shredder and the Foot Clan and forced to create two mutants to fight the Turtles. Bound and Gagged: After being kidnapped by the Foot Clan, there are two instances where Perry is shown bound and gagged. During the second instance, he gets rescued by Donatello after the latter crashes through a roof as a result of being thrown away by Tokka. Canon Foreigner: He was created for the second movie and never appeared in the comics. Friend to All Living Things: Even knowing what Shredder wanted to do with Tokka and Rahzar, he begged Shredder not to kill the two mutants when they proved "intellectually inferior" and had them demonstrate they had other useful abilities to save them. Expy: Professor Perry is something of amuch more benevolentBaxter Stockman.

characters.name: Keno
characters.description: A pizza delivery boy that studied martial arts, he eventually ran into the turtles and befriended them. Badass Normal: Not as skilled as the turtles in martial arts, but he's able to fight off a couple of thugs robbing a store."Did I mention I studied martial arts?" Big Damn Heroes: Keno kicks away the ooze canister from Shredder's hand so that Perry can retrieve it during the second film's climax. Canon Foreigner: Keno has no counterpart elsewhere in the franchise, at best substituting for Casey Jones in the second film alone. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Does not return for the third film.

characters.name: Kenshin
characters.description: The son of Lord Norinaga from the past, he finds himself dragged to the present when the time staff switches him with April O'Neil. Calling the Old Man Out: Kenshin does this towards his father.Lord Norinaga:Kenshin, I have forbid you for leaving the palace. You have disgraced me.Kenshin:It isyouwho have disgraced me, father. You and your unjust war.[Everyone is quiet.Norinaga is about to come down hard on him until Walker arrives.] Canon Foreigner: He was created for the third movie and never appeared in the comics. Dating What Daddy Hates: Norinaga is at war with Mitsu because he doesn't approve of his son's relationship with her. Fainting: The first time he saw Splinter and lampshaded in the third film.Don:Youdohave that affect on people, master.

characters.name: Whit
characters.description: Big Damn Heroes: Towards the end of the film, Whit uses a cannonball to sendWalkerplunging to his watery death. Canon Foreigner: He was created for the third movie and never appeared in the comics. Generation Xerox: Implied to be the ancestor of Casey Jones and, as such, is played by the same actor and is attracted to April. Heel–Face Turn: Whit starts off working with Walker, but eventually switches sides after being betrayed towards the end of the film. Hired Guns: Was a mercenary hired by Walker before he incited a mutiny against him.

characters.name: Mitsu
characters.description: Bow and Sword in Accord: Bow and knife actually. Canon Foreigner: She was created for the third movie and never appeared in the comics. Interspecies Romance: With Mikey during the third movie, but chose not to pursue the relationship because of her commitment to Kenshin. But he wanted to stay with her anyway. Reverse Grip: Mitsu holds her dagger this way. Star-Crossed Lovers: With Kenshin.

characters.name: Yoshi
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: He was created for the third movie and never appeared in the comics. Intergenerational Friendship: With Raph. Interspecies Friendship: Also with Raph.

characters.name: Chief Sterns
characters.description: The Chief of the New York City Police Department, he has the misfortune of being the one in charge of putting a stop to the Foot Clan's reign of terror in the city. Berserk Button: The mere insinuation that April was bossing him around led him to shout her out of his office. Brooklyn Rage: Has shades of it. Canon Foreigner: He was created for these movies and never appeared in the comics. Da Chief: Self-explanatory. Unusually, rather than aCowboy Cophe chews out, it's investigative reporter April O'Neil.

characters.name: Shredder
characters.description: A powerful crime lord and leader of the Foot Clan. His true identity is Oroku Saki, the man responsible for killing Splinter's mentor/owner, Hamato Yoshi. Adaptational Badass: Shredder in this continuity is depicted as an unstoppableJuggernaut, as opposed to being an easily defeatedStarter Villainin the comics and anIneffectual Sympathetic Villainin the cartoon series (though the cartoon generally showed that Shreddercoulddefeat the Turtles themselves in combat; being able to prevent them from stopping hisplans, on the other hand...). Most subsequent Shredders have followed the film's example. Adaptational Modesty: Shredder worea sleeveless outfitinthe original comicsandthe 1987 animated series. By contrast, he has sleeves in these movies. Big Bad: He is this for the first two films. Characterization Marches On: In the second film, he is much more prone to dramatics and hammy declarations owing to the film leaning more on the influence of the cartoon.

characters.name: Tatsu
characters.description: Shredder'sDragonand second-in-command of the Foot Clan. Bald of Evil: Not a hair on his head and the second-in-command to the Shredder. Canon Foreigner: He originated in the films. Canon Immigrant: Had an appearance as a boss inThe Hyperstone Heistand later appears as a major villain inthe 2012 cartoon. Combat Pragmatist: Boots one of his Foot Ninja in the face when he bows to him after a duel. He frames it as anEvil Mentormoment though, telling the kid that he should never lower his eyes to an enemy.

characters.name: Freddy
characters.description: A fresh-faced newsboy working at Channel 3 news. He's secretly a spy for the Foot Clan. Canon Foreigner: He was created for the second movie and never appeared in the comics. Mauve Shirt: Freddy fares better than the other Foot Ninja mooks, due to also being April's co-worker and the one to alert Shredder to the effects of the ooze. The Mole: Sent to spy on April, who eventually finds out.

characters.name: Lord Norinaga
characters.description: Abusive Parent: Downplayed, as he only expressed his disappointment at his son for disobeying him, though he nearly came down hard on Kenshin just forcalling him out on his "unjust war" in front of everyone. But deep down he truly cares for his son, the problem is that he disapproves his son's relationship with Mitsu for some reason.At the end, he was happy to have his son back (and accepted his relationship with Mitsu). Big Bad Duumvirate: With Walker. Norinaga agrees to an alliance with Walker so he can use their firearms on his enemies, though Walker is the more malevolent of the pair. Canon Foreigner: He was created for the third movie and never appeared in the comics. Defeat Means Respect:Thoroughly humbled after his sword fight with Leo. It's shown when Norinaga and Mitsu have made peace with each other. Evil Is Petty: The only reason he's at war with Mitsu is because he doesn't approve of her son's relationship with her. Thus he believes she kidnapped Kenshin just to spite him.

characters.name: Walker
characters.description: Arbitrary Skepticism: He doesn't believe for a second that April is a witch who "spirited away" his son. But his first encounter with the Ninja Turtles has left him mystified. Arms Dealer: Provides Noringo with his guns and cannons. Big Bad Duumvirate: With Norinaga, who agrees to an alliance with Walker so he can use their firearms on his enemies. Although in this case, Walker is the more malevolent of the pair. Canon Foreigner: He was created for the third movie and never appeared in the comics. Disney Villain Death:Walker plunges to his watery doom at the end of the third film.Don:Bungie-jumping without a bungie. That could be dangerous.

characters.name: Niles
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: He was created for the third movie and never appeared in the comics. Politically Incorrect Villain: A minor case, he calls the Honor Guards (Turtles in disguise) "ugly lump of dungs" and the dungeon keeper "fatso-san". Running Gag: Being on the receiving end of the Turtles' wet willies. He gives one to himself before running away. Speech Impediment: Speaks with a lisp.Don:(to Niles, after Raph scares him off)Later, Popeye! Terrible Trio: With two other guys.

characters.name: Rebecca Vincent
characters.description: Da Chief: She's the Police Chief. Friend on the Force: Becomes this. Reasonable Authority Figure: She's portrayed as a bit of aBitch in Sheep's Clothingat first but gradually evolves into this at the latter end of the film, setting April and Casey free when April's innocence was finally proven and even deciding to overlook the fact that Casey had stolen her cell phone in order to prove their innocence. Her attitude towards the TMNT also evolves, seeing them as monsters at first but eventually coming to see them as heroes.

characters.name: Eric Sacks
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He initially seems like a nice, reasonable businessman who publicly opposes the Foot Clan's actions, but under the surface,he's aCorrupt Corporate Executivewho works as the Shredder'sDragon, and freely admits that his only motive for trying to poison New York is to make himself "stupid rich." But Not Too Foreign: An American who was born in Japan. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He is completely left out of the 2016 sequel, without so much as a mention. Corrupt Corporate Executive: HisEvil Planamounts to releasing alethal biotoxinupon New York just so he can profit from making an antidote. Cut Lex Luthor a Check: He has a building in downtown Manhattan, a mansion home outside of town, helicopter, resources to have labs - but he's evidently not richenough. He wants to be "stupid rich" bypoisoning the city and selling the cure.

characters.name: Dr. Baxter Stockman
characters.description: Ambition Is Evil: Baxter's motivation for helping Shredder and Krang is to be remembered in a way that makes other famous scientist footnotes in history. Black and Nerdy: So nerdy that he knows thedifference between a "nerd" and a "geek." Chronic Backstabbing Disorder:Becomes a victim of this when Shredder decides he doesn't need his help anymore. For Science!: Jazzed about helping Shredder create his own mutants. Glory Seeker: He dreams of being remembered as a great scientific trailblazer.ShredderKicks The Dogby having Baxter dragged off to imprisonment once he'soutlived his usefulnessand assuring him that no one will ever even know his name.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: Adaptational Wimp: Due to having far less experience in combat, as well as how their primary form of training came from watching martial arts movies, the Turtles are far less coordinated in fights than they are in most adaptations. Notably, they barely scrape a victory against a group of normal thugs running a chop shop early in the film, something that other incarnations of the Turtles would have no issues with. Beware the Silly Ones: These mutant teens may be lovable dorks who only want to fit in, but they're still highly trained ninjas. They were able to handle local crime gangs on their own and saved New York from a colossal super mutant. Brought to You by the Letter "S": They all wear belts bearing their initials on them. Calling Parents by Their Name: While the Turtles mostly refer to Splinter as "dad" in this version, Leo refers to him by his name twice, likemost incarnations.Leo:We're sorry, Splinter. The guys wanted to see a movie. I tried to talk 'em out of it. Charles Atlas Superpower: ThoughDownplayed,Talesreferences that every Mutant has at least some degree of enhanced strength as a common feature, which is part of the reason the teenagers are able to fight with adults andacrobatically leap across rooftopsto get around. Whilst still not as muscular as some of their prior incarnations, this passive strength allows them to do some things like dent metal and grapple with theMechazoids, even if they're on the losing side sansRaph.

characters.name: Superfly
characters.description: The leader of the mutant gang who has become a feared criminal in the city. Adapted Out: Not Superfly himself,but the junior novelization ends before it gets to the part where he becomesSuperDuperFly, with the only hint being that the Turtles and the mutants are prepared to deal with him again when he returns. Affably Evil: He initially starts out this way when he first meets the Turtles, being surprisingly amicable and genuinely friendly with them with him even declaring them as cousins. He unfortunately loses this by the end of the film once the Turtles and the rest of his reformed gang go against his genocidal plans. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: He displays this rare moment when the combined pushback of his crew and Turtles actually get pin him against the controls of his machine. He pleads with the bystanding Splinter, hoping to get him to understand his extremist motives and implicitly provide backup in calling off Splinter's rebellious kids. Ax-Crazy: He is more than willing to kill anyone who are unlucky enough to face his wrath or get in the way of his goals.He getsworsewhen he becomesSuperDuperFly.

characters.name: Genghis Frog
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: While the Punk Frogs did start out as enemies of the Turtles, they were manipulated by Shredder into fighting them. Here, Genghis Frog is a member of Superfly's gang.It turns out that he is actually closer to his original interpretation, being initially led down the wrong path by Superfly before the Turtles convince him that he can be better. Adapted Out: He's not accompanied by the other Punk Frogs. Atrocious Alias:Superfly's not jazzedabout how a very American frog has a random Mongolian epithet. Frog Men: He’s a Mutant frog. Furry Reminder:When fighting Superfly, he lashes out with his tongue and sticks it on Superfly much like an actual frog hunting flies. The difference is that, since Superfly is obviously too big to pull in his mouth, Genghis pulls himself in towards Superfly and delivers a body slam.

characters.name: Ray Fillet
characters.description: Actor Allusion: He's voiced byPost Malone, so of course he's going to try and sing every chance he gets. Adaptation Species Change: Originally, he was a human-turned-mutant, but here, he originated from a mutated manta embryo. (Though his IDW version started as a normal manta) Adaptational Villainy: He is usually an ally of the Turtles and a mutant hero. This time he seems to have taken a more villainous role as a member of Superfly's gang.Like the other members of Superfly's gang, he pulls aHeel–Face Turnafter the Turtles get through to him. Beautiful Singing Voice: He can sing pretty well for a giant mutant ray, but is mainly into singing his own name. Beware My Stinger Tail: Natch, being a ray.One way he uses it is to trip up Superfly with it while he's occupied with Mikey, Raph, and Leatherhead.

characters.name: Scumbug
characters.description: Adaptation Species Change: Earlier versions of Scumbug were human-born, this version started as a cockroach embryo. As Himself: Scumbug's teaser poster describes her this way. According to the filmmakers, this was a mistake — it was supposed to read "asherself". Creepy Cockroach: She's a mutant cockroach, and to be brutally honest, she isn’t really known for her looks. Gender Flip: She's a female mutant in this continuity. In the movie, April refers to her as a "cockroach lady", andSplinter refers to her as a woman and falls in love with her by the end of the film. Intelligible Unintelligible: Although she speaks in random garbling sounds, Splinter can understand her just fine (implied to be because he befriended a cockroach when he was a normal rat).

characters.name: East River Three
characters.description: A group created due to Superfly's machine falling into the ocean, turning three of the fish there into mutants. Anti-Villain: The group's motivation is that they just want to reclaim the Pearl stolen from their home to be accepted again.Lee and Sally also aren't privy to the worst parts of Goldfin's plan, and when the truth of Goldfin's villainy becomes apparent, help the Turtles. Canon Foreigner: The group and its members were created for this continuity, and have no existing counterparts in priorTMNTmedia. Inexplicably Awesome: All of them have been mutants for three weeks tops and despite the Turtles and Splinter being given theAdaptational Wimptreatment to a degree in this continuity, they've still been training in the fighting arts for much longer. Despite all that, the East River Three can still give the Turtles and Splinter a very difficult time in battle, particularly whenGoldfin takes on and defeats the Turtles in their climactic battle, displaying dizzying levels of agility and skill to take the four out. While Lee'sShock and Awepowers would logically make her a threat power-wise, there's absolutely no rhyme or reason for them being able to fight like absolute pros, considering how they haven't even been mutants for a month and have gotten no formal training in anything... but somehow, they're just that good in spite of the odds. Misplaced Wildlife: Despite originating from the East River, electric eels, sea horses, goldfish, and sea anemones are not native there much less can even survive there. Sea anemones and sea horses require salt water with the latter requiring also warm tropical water to survive. Electric eels live in the warm tropical rivers of South America.Justifiedin the case of Goldfin. While the domestic goldfish’s wild ancestors originate in South China, people inReal Lifedo release their pet goldfish into nonnative temperate rivers and lakes where they can thrive.

characters.name: The Monster Mutanimals
characters.description: A group of mass-produced mutated animals created by scientist Jordan Perry in his efforts to replicate Baxter Stockman's mutagen, consisting of mutated turtles, wolves, snakes, worms, and ants. Several of the turtle and wolf mutants have named themselves "Tokka" and "Rahzar", respectively. In addition, the snakes, worms, and ants named themselves "Scale Tail", "Wyrm", and "Antrax", respectively. Adaptational Intelligence: Tokka and Rahzar tend to be portrayed asvery lackingin intelligence and easily manipulated, but both in this adaptation are smarter than the other mass-produced mutant animals to the point of being able to speak coherently, and are capable of openly scheming against their creator, Jordan Perry. Alleged Lookalikes: At least one Tokka would frequent a pizzeria to take advantage of the owners giving the Turtles free pizza as thanks for saving the city. When the actual Turtles (sans Donatello) visit, the owner tells them off for that Tokka's behavior under the belief it was the brothers causing trouble, moments before the Tokka responsible for the owner's grievances arrives to fight the Turtles. Body Horror: The mutant worm species' transformation was not a very pretty one, with it having multiple tongues sticking out of its perpetually-open mouth. Composite Character: Rahzar heavily resembles his 2012 incarnation in having a slimmer build and more agile fighting style, with a similar level of intelligence, but is a mutated wolf rather than being initially human and is prominently partnered with Tokka, more like the earliest incarnations of the characters in the 1990 films and 1987 cartoon.

characters.name: Scratch
characters.description: Scratch is a one eyed mutant cat and self-proclaimed nemesis of the turtles. Badly Battered Babysitter: His attempts on Splinter were thwarted by the turtles as babies, who wanted to play with him, but were being too rough with him. Composite Character: His name is Scratch, after the character from the 1987 cartoon's toyline, but his connection to Splinter and the Turtles prior to their mutations and hislost eyewhich he covers with an eyepatch, give him a resemblance to the IDW Comics' character Old Hob. Embarrassed by a Child: Within a year after his mutation, Scratch tried multiple times to get Splinter, but is thwarted by the turtles, who had no idea at the time. Eye Scream: Much like Old Hob, who Scratch is partly based on, he had his right eye scratched out by Splinter prior to his mutation.

characters.name: Rod Underwood Jr.
characters.description: Bishop's put-upon intern who was forced on her by his father in exchange for funding, to try and encourage him to figure out what he wants to do with his life. Artistic License – Biology: He calls his eyes of mismatched colors "anisocoria" rather than heterochromia.Season 2 has Michelangelo correct him on it, which slightly upsets Rod due to the stress of everything going on at that point. Dumbass Has a Point:He was never meant to be portrayed as particularly bright (not just comparing to Bishop). He does, however, come up with the idea of "turning them off" (meaning the Mechazoids). After being briefly berated by Bishop, Donatello then explains that an EMP could knock them out and stop the destruction. He also convinces Bishop to let the Turtles into their control room when the Mechazoids present themselves as a threat to everybody.He's surprisingly quick to see through Bishop's rhetoric about "defending humanity" and surmise that she actually just wants revenge against the Turtles forthe loss of her life's work. He was never meant to be portrayed as particularly bright (not just comparing to Bishop). He does, however, come up with the idea of "turning them off" (meaning the Mechazoids). After being briefly berated by Bishop, Donatello then explains that an EMP could knock them out and stop the destruction. He also convinces Bishop to let the Turtles into their control room when the Mechazoids present themselves as a threat to everybody. He's surprisingly quick to see through Bishop's rhetoric about "defending humanity" and surmise that she actually just wants revenge against the Turtles forthe loss of her life's work.

characters.name: Rod Underwood Sr.
characters.description: Bishop's financial backer for Bishop Robotics. Abusive Parents: It would be understating it to say that he treats his three children horribly, to the point he is responsible for all of theirFreudian Excuses. A flashback of their younger days shows he stole Rod Jr.'s dessert and denied his kindly butler permission to give him a replacement all in the name of teaching his son a lesson.His habit of stealing from his children did not go away even when the trio became adults. Adaptational Villainy:Prior adaptations of Muckman tend to be on the side of the Turtles, whereas Rod Underwood Sr. seeks to become a mutant for the sake of power. Breaking Old Trends: He's the first character in theMutant Mayhemcontinuityto be mutated from a human being rather than being anUplifted Animallike most of the others. Canon Character All Along: The final episode ofTalesreveals him to bea reimagining of Muckman.

characters.name: Dr. Maude Underwood
characters.description: CEO of the the scientific research company known as Null Group. Dumber Than They Look: Despite being CEO of a huge research company, she has no idea how said company works or even many basic scientific terms. When one of the Null Group workers lists Maude's father being rich as the reasoning for her being labeled as a doctor, it's not out of priority or specifics, so much as it is theonlyreason. She is literally a doctor in name only! Earn Your Happy Ending:After a life of wanting the approval of her abusive father and acting as a figurehead for Null Group, Maude lives a far more relaxed life as a barista using the coffee recipe she made to earn success. Freudian Excuse: Her father made no attempt to reign in her and Todd's bullying of Rod Jr. and cared more about teaching his children about needing to be at the top to explain much of Maude's standoffish behavior anddesire to be the favorite child. Must Have Caffeine: The only actual achievement she makes during her time as CEO is perfecting a coffee recipe she constantly drinks,and shebecomes a baristaafter her father's defeat.

characters.name: Todd Underwood
characters.description: A fitness trainer with a passion for animals. The Atoner:Becomes a protector of endangered species after his father's defeat. Badass Normal: He's able to square off on even footing with the Turtles. Bait the Dog: He initially seems a lot more laid-back and friendly than his siblings. Then it turns out he wants to eat Leatherhead to become a mutant. Earn Your Happy Ending:After a life of wanting the approval of his abusive father and having less than altruistic reasonings for his fitness coaching, he converts his business to an endangered species protection group.

characters.name: Tobias "Toby" Scanlon
characters.description: CEOof Mac-N-Dronez and owner of the Coexisting Center. Hidden Disdain Reveal: Young Entrepreneur: Said to have gotten rich in his mid-20s.

characters.name: Emilie
characters.description: A girl with a prosthetic leg training to be in the Paralympics. Appeal to Familial Wisdom: She learnt Qigong from her grandfather. Artificial Limbs: She has a prosthetic left leg. Tomboy: She has a shaved head. Willfully Weak: A previous coach criticized her for her dream of being in the Paralympics.

characters.name: Sai Modi
characters.description: Donnie's friend and scientist.

characters.name: Alshon
characters.description: Quest Giver: He tells the turtles about Mewbie troubles he hears from customers and would reward them in taste testing drinks if dealt with. Too Smart for Education: He dropped out of college to become a barrista, which his father didn't realize.

characters.name: Ian
characters.description: High school student, friend of Donatello and member of Robotics Club. Brainy Brunet: Like Irma, Ian not only has brown hair, but has enough knowledge to be in the school's Robotics Club. Floating in a Bubble: He swims with floaties on.

characters.name: Bad Bernie
characters.description: One of the criminals connected to Superfly, later affiliates with Goldfin. Alliterative Name:BadBernie Animal Motifs: His buck teeth and unkempt design gives him a resemblance to a rat, due to his design having been initially meant for an adaptation of the Rat King. Arc Villain: Shares this role with Goldfin, being one of the main antagonists of the second arc ofTales, planning to sell the Pearl for a massive profit. Ascended Extra: He's defeated in the space of a montage inMutant Mayhemand gets very little expansion on his character, but is one of theArc VillainsinTales.

characters.name: The Crime Ring Heads
characters.description: The criminals running the crime ring that is connected with Superfly and his plans. Alliterative Name: The named crime bosses all have names following this pattern. Curb-Stomp Battle: Their goons end up suffering this at the hands of the Turtles. Dirty Coward: Besides the Chop Shop Boss who joins his goons in fighting the Turtles, the other crime bosses aren't shown fighting with Normal Nate fleeing in terror from Raphael. Equal-Opportunity Evil: Bald Bronson is an African-American man while Short Sharon is an Asian woman.

characters.name: Jordan Perry
characters.description: A scientist who aims to create a version of Baxter Stockman's mutagen, creating the Monster Mutanimals in his experiments. Adaptational Villainy: So so much, the original is not as malevolent as this incarnation of the character. The original version fromSecret of the Oozeis a benevolent scientist who is forced by Shredder to do vile experiments, meanwhile theMutant Mayhemversion is a willing mad scientist that is essentially the opposite of the original version. Ambiguous Situation:He is eaten by the mutant created from his own DNA, shown coming out of its remains, only to be attacked by another one of his experiments, with the story arc'sFraming Deviceof Donatello and Irma making a VR game coming back to show the last bit was part of said game. With this in mind, whether or not Jordan was killed when he was eaten and the adventure on Staten Island gave Donny and Irma the inspiration to make him the player character of the game, or the entire adventure (and thus Jordan himself) was just made up as the story of the VR game is left unclear. Bad People Abuse Animals: A flashback depicting one of the early days of his mutagen experiments shows him giving mutagen to an animal from a supply of the same species, it exploding, and him repeating once more. The flashback having him stand behind glass implies this was a recurring trend. He doesn't treat the Monster Mutanimals much better, keeping a remote just to blow them up. Foil: To Baxter Stockman. Both wanted to mutate animals, but Baxter had benevolent reasons for doing so compared to Jordan's self-serving ones. The flashback showing them meeting has Jordansquish a flywith Baxter frowning in response, further highlighting how different the two are from each other in terms of personality and intent.

characters.name: Angel
characters.description: Adaptational Early Appearance: She notably appears before Casey Jones, a character she's associated with in the 2003 cartoon and IDW comics, in this incarnation. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: Angel and Hun are romantically involved in this incarnation. Adaptational Villainy: Since this version is the leader of the Purple Dragons, she's a lot more vicious than her previous counterparts. Composite Character: Her irritable temperament and leadership position (albeit shared) in the Purple Dragons are more evocative of traditional incarnations of Hun. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Despite her vicious nature, she deeply cares for her comrades including her boyfriend Hun. Comforting him when the chickens get killed offscreen after letting them free and concerned for Cane when Lee pulls down and yanks her in the surface of the store.

characters.name: Kitsune
characters.description: A crime boss who employs the Purple Dragons, and effectively the de facto leader of the gang. Adaptational Mundanity: She's a shape-shifting witch and a member of the Pantheon in her original appearance. Here, she's just a normal human crime boss with no apparent powers. Bad Boss: Kitsune ignores Angel’s warnings, intimidates Hun, and treats her staff as disposable. The Dreaded: Kitsune terrifies Hun with her quiet stare. In Name Only: She has very little in common with the IDW character she’s named after.

characters.name: Spuds
characters.description: A gym instructor and secret Purple Dragon member. Adaptational Context Change: While still a Purple Dragon, Spuds isn't a thug. Instead he's a gym trainer. He's also aAdaptational Nice Guycompared to his 2003 iteration. But he also displaysAdaptational Intelligenceat being able to sway Raph to Kitsune. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Spuds acts as a reasonable trainer to Raph, helping him train and listening to his rants. But in actuality is a member of the Purple Dragons, whose been manipulating him. Canon Immigrant: Spuds is originally from the Mirage Comics and the 2003 cartoon, who was also a Purple Dragon there. Edible Theme Naming: His nicknamed 'Spuds', because potatoes are his mother's favorite food.

characters.name: Cammy Leon
characters.description: A mutant chameleon who wants a world full of mutants. Even Evil Has Standards: When asked what will happen to the humans in her city of mutants, she stated that they can live in the suburbs, which as Donnetello puts it, a step up from Superfly's plan. Foil: In more ways than one, she's a lot like Superfly, they both hated humanity and wanted a world only for mutants, but while Superfly never had aHeel–Face Turnunlike his family, Cammy had one after her former captors captures the rampaging mewbies. Nice Girl: After herHeel–Face Turn, Cammy and the turtles team up and plan how to stop the pheromones and save the mewbies from TCRI, she looked up what guest should do to show kindness and she cleaned their living room. One-Winged Angel:After Cammy tries to go back into the exploding pheromone factory to save the mewbies that got left behind, Cammy got supercharged and turned into the fast and feral Turbo Cammy.

characters.name: Cynthia Utrom
characters.description: The mysterious head of TCRI. Ambiguously Human: Her name, appearance, and voice all indicate that she's an Utrom in disguise, likely even Krang himself, but never reveals herself in the actual film. Notably, she hasn't visibly aged in 15 years unlike Splinter or her Squad Leader. Composite Character: She visually resembles and sounds like Krang fromthe 1987 cartoon(although Krang was not originally an Utrom, he was a disembodied brain of an alien warlord from Dimension X and hence resembled the Utroms), but her goal of trying to milk the Turtles and make supersoldiers using the mutagen in their bloodstream is similar to that of Agent Bishop fromthe 2003 cartoon. Her being the head of TCRI, using"Utrom" as her last nameandhaving purple hairis also similar toMr. Mortufrom the 2003 series. Corrupt Corporate Executive: She's the executive of a scientific corporation seeking to capture the Turtles and drain them dry of all their blood so she can recreate Stockman's mutagen and create an army of mutant super-soldiers to sell off to the highest bidder. And she doesn't care if she has to kill four teenagers in order to do it. Electric Torture: When the Turtles speak out in any way, she simply responds with the press of a button that delivers an electric shock to them.

characters.name: Squad Leader
characters.description: Cynthia's main enforcer of TCRI's attempts to capture any of Stockman's mutants. All There in the Manual: He remains unnamed in the movie, but the end credits of the movie and the junior novelization refer to him as "Spider". The Dragon: He's Cynthia's main muscle on the ground when tracking down and subduing the mutants for TCRI's purposes, and isthe primary oppositionthe Turtles face when TCRI's attempt to track Superfly leads to them capturing the teens instead. Eyepatch of Power: In the opening scene, he loses his left eye after getting attacked by the young Superfly. He wears an eyepatch over it in the present day. Expy: Hun fromthe 2003 cartoon, another blonde muscularDragon. Although, he is a lot smaller than the7 feet tall Hun.

characters.name: Bishop
characters.description: A mysterious woman with a hatred of mutants. Adaptation Name Change: Her name is "Josefina", to tie into herGender Flipfrom prior adaptations usually named John Bishop. Adaptational Early Appearance: Bishop becomes a threat to the Turtles shortly afterMutant Mayhem, making her one of their earliest rogues in this adaptation, over prior incarnations' tendency to appear much later than Shredder in the Turtles' lives. Adaptational Intelligence: Bishop is an inventor in this incarnation, something that prior adaptations of the characters seemingly had little ability to do, and had to rely on others. Adaptational Job Change: Bishop is trying to make a robotics company in this incarnation, and does not work for the Earth Protection Force.The end of the arc features her becoming a member of the Earth Protection Force, but unlike prior adaptations' leadership role, she's providing Mechazoids to them now.

characters.name: Mechazoids
characters.description: Bishop's mechanical soldiers, which she created initially to benefit mankind, but turned into a weapon to hunt down the Turtles. Adaptive Ability: Bishop designed them to learn and constantly adapt to their situations.This leads to them adapting their programming to decide that, since all life is capable of mutation, then all life must be destroyed. It also allows them to reject Bishop's shutdown commands. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Donatello frequently compliments Bishop's work on the Mechazoids, but just as often notes that their code could use improvement, with the arc they're in demonstrating that they have problems distinguishing between mutants and benign mutations (such as Rod's heterochromia),and the Mechazoids eventually decide that they shouldn't listen to Bishop anymore to eradicate humanity to prevent them frompossiblybecoming mutants. The Assimilator: Their means of repairing any damage to themselves involves finding and absorbing any nearby technology, assuming their characteristics in the process. Awesomeness by Analysis: 01 learns Ninjitsu by just observing Leonardo fight it.

characters.name: Detective Hauser
characters.description: Freudian Excuse: He was swarmed by a flock of pigeons in his youth, resulting in his hatred of birds as an adult. Motivated by Fear: A massive ornithophobic, Hauser has the police concentrate on hunting down Pigeon Pete rather than evacuate the citizens from the flood after being massively defecated on. Skewed Priorities: He obsesses over catching Pigeon Pete even when it's clearthat the pump station he's in is about to explode.

characters.name: Chrome Dome
characters.description: Adaptational Backstory Change: From a robot constructed by Shredder to an AI-powered toymaker with no connection to Shredder. Corrupted Character Copy: He is an obvious copy of Man-E-Faces with the face swapping of his toy and himself and robotic looking in nature, with a major difference of the two being the opposite alignments. Power Copying: Chrome Dome is able to copy whatever ability he sees. The Turtles exploit this against him by only copying terrible moves that harm and destroy himself. Riddle for the Ages: Whoever created Chrome Dome is the biggest mystery that was never solved and their intentions are unknown. Self-Deprecation: His advertisement of the Tubular Tortoise Karate Warriors has himself as the bad guy being beaten up by the titular Warriors and he does not go towards depicting himself as the hero who beats up evil turtles, which does show some level of humility.

characters.name: Zayton Honeycutt/Fugitoid
characters.description: Child Prodigy: He was hired by the EPF before he could graduate from Eastman High. Mythology Gag: Like his Roninverse counterpart, Zayton was a human from Earth.
